There are few whistles and bells to this device, but what there is is functionality. I was looking for a way to connect my iphone/laptop to my stereo system to free my music. This device did the job admirably. I can now enjoy my digital music libraries wirelessly from iTunes. Also, I have fed audio for Netflix through it to to get a fuller sound. For functionality, you cannot beat the price.

This really is a beautiful laptop, elegantly designed with a rich, quality feel to it. The bottom of the laptop has an almost suede like feel to it and the packaging only enhances the feel of luxury. It doesn't seem to fully fulfill the requirements of an ultrabook, it is definitely an aesthetically elegant machine.

As for Specs, the i5 with 500 Gig hard drive is plenty beefy, especially at the price that Amazon is selling this for. It would be nice to have a little more memory but that is an easy upgrade. We have used this for light gaming, mostly mine craft and it handles that with no problem. I don't know that this would be a stellar gaming laptop though, but it is a rock solid personal laptop.

The biggest problem I have with it, is my own personal frustrations over windows 8. I'm getting there with familiarity, but still having problems with Microsoft having spent decades teaching us how to navigate and work with computers to have them arbitrarily take easy control from us. But that's a rant for another time.

I have to admit that windows 8 looks sharp and stellar on this machine. The video is clear and crisp. We have watched streamed videos and they are great, with no lag.

I really can't say enough about the look and feel. That and the very decent specs make this a great priced laptop at around $700.

I was intrigued by the two part case, with the snap on back and removable "smart cover." They separate easily and leave the Air with a nice feeling snap on back protector. With the cover on, I was a little disappointed that it is not truly a smart cover as it does not control powering the Air on and off. This is a nice feature with other cases I have had for my earlier iPad2.

The stand features work ok. The landscape taller stand configuration is good for watching hulu etc. The flatter configuration would probably be good if you are one of those who type directly onto the iPad (I don't/can't). All in all it is a decent cover, although I prefer some of the other Belkin covers I had for the iPad2.

I continue to be impressed with the AmazonBasics line. They are true to their name that they are basic, but they have all been very decent products. This bag is no different, it is solid and has everything you would expect in a good Camera Bag but no extra whistles and bells. It was exactly what I was looking for and carries a decent price tag.

The one concern is that it is listed as a large gadget bag. I don't know that I would classify it as large as it is big enough to carry a single dslr with a couple of lenses and a hand full of filters and gadgets. It is actually just the standard base camera kit bag. So it has enough room to do a day trip, but don't look to deeply into the "Large" in the description.

I have actually made this into my birding grab bag and field library. It fits 5 specialty field guides, my binoculars, a small first aid kit, lense cleaning supplies, and a couple of candy bars. It is perfect for grabbing and tossing in the car for emergency field identifications and to keep my birding accessories handy and organized.

I really like this speaker system. My other speakers are iPod specific so it is nice to have one that takes just a mini stereo, although it leaves you with the dilemna of where to put an iPod when you connect it. I also like the indoor outdoor options, although this is definitely not a weather proof solution.

The sound is very nice although directional so it sounds a little tinny if you are not directly in line with the speakers.

Pros
+ Universal
+ Nice Design
+ Easy Controls
+ nice sound
+ optional battery power

Cons
- No great place to mount an attached ipod

I was looking for a docking station for my sons iPod 5th Generation since the change in connectors has invalidated all my older docking stations for him. This Dock fills the bill nearly perfectly. The sound is very nice and the controls are very easy. My son is very happy with it and it fills his room with sound well but does not overpower the entire home.

I downloaded the app and found it to be just OK. I don't know that I'll use it and actually favor the software for my Phillips Dock over this, although that one is far from perfect as well. Otherwise the unit top controls worked fine to control the docked iPod. The build materials seem pretty solid. A couple of disappointments, there is no remote and the connector is too short to work with most cases. Neither my sons iPod, nor my iPhone will connect to the dock without removing our cases first which is a little annoying. I have not had this issue with my older docks with the wider connection, although I guess I've never had such thick cases as we have now.

Pros
+ Good Sound
+ Completely Plug and Play (although you can add an app if you want)

Cons
- Connector not long enough to work with iPod or iPhone Cases on.
- App for the dock is just OK, there is room for improvement.

All in all, it is a decent dock for the price. My son is very happy with it, other than the fact the connector does not work with our cases.

Well, the price is about right for what you get. It's a no whistles or bells plastic cover that holds my iPad mini well and does protect the back well and provides a screen protector for the front. I can't really rant or rave about it, but I can say that you get value for the price.

It does have a little weight which takes away from the Mini's unbelievable lightness, but being clear it does nothing to take away from the mini's elegant lines. I plan to go back to a book type cover though for a little extra protection from the rigors of life in a messenger bag, but the price is almost worth the screen protector alone.

I have three main uses for tripods, food photography, nature photography and to hold up a spotting scope. This tripod succeeds wonderfully at two of those. It is great for nature photography and supporting the spotting scope. I am 6' 3" and I love that height of this tripod. even without extending the center post, I can comfortably use the tripod when standing.

This is a fantastic birdwatching tripod for my spotting scope. The carbon fiber material is light and rugid. Vanguard has remembered the little things, for example, the upper legs are padded which is huge in when trying to spot an owl in Minnesota at twenty below. The insulation makes the tripod much more comfortable to handle, equally when shooting images of Northern lights.

The legs are fairly sturdy although I feel that here is a little more play in the carbon fiber over my older aluminum, Bogen tripod. I was a little disappointed that there are just a few angle settings for the legs. They click into 30 and about 60 degrees. It would be nice to have more granular settings, so I find myself altering leg lengths more than my other tripod. The feet are well designed with hard steel spikes with nice rubber feet for indoor uses. Both options allow for good stable footings.

Also there are some great other details like leveling bubbles on the top of the tripod and ball head. Also, I like that they though to include a hook at the bottom of the center post for adding stability weights. The leg releases are easy to use and have held tight during all my time in the field with the tripod.

Where I wish they had put more into this tripod is the ball head. It doesn't seem to live up to the tripod body. I miss a pan handle and while I appreciate the feel and functionality of the locking knobs, it just seems like it is not the pro quality of the rest of the tripod. There is a second leveling bubble on the head itself which is fantastic. But probably the biggest drawback is the quick release plate. It is not quick at all, it requires quite a bit of screwing with thumbscrew to attach. Also there is not set screw on the "quick" release plate.

Pros
+ Height
+ padded legs for comfort in cold weather
+ Light Weight
+ Great feet, both the grippy robber shoes and the steel spikes
+ built in leveling bubbles
+ Functional and strong leg locks
+ built in hook on bottom of center post
+ Second leveling bubble on the head

Cons
- No built in strap
- Carrying case is ok (this is more a neutral than a con)
- the head is not great
- limited leg angles
- Head could be better
- Somewhat awkward and slow quick release plates
- Lacks a panning arm.

In General, this is an awesome tripod, but for the money I would have expected a little more, especially a strap and a better head unit. But I have to admit I love this tripod. I would have put 4.5 stars if possible, but for $500 my expectation for a "Professional" tripod head is a little higher. But for my uses it's awesome, it holds the Spotting Scope will but again, lack of a panning arm hinders it. From the shoulders down, the best I've seen.

I truly love these headphones for style. They are a little bulky but you can tell that style was high on the designer's list. I have been using a pair of Sennheiser headphones exclusively and I feel that the sound on these are a little crisper and the sound canceling is comparable. I have no complaints at all on the corded sound these produce. I'm a little less happy with the Bluetooth which works well when close to the bluetooth source and have a line of sight between the two. These work beautifully when listening to books on tape on walks - perhaps a little too well and cutting me off from the environment.

I do wish they would fold up a little smaller, so Sennheiser will continue to be my traveling headphones, but these have found a place wired to my computer for late night music and video enjoyment. The price is a little high for dedicated wired headphones though.

I liked the idea of getting a little added protection for my 40D and this case does protect it a little bit. However most of the protection is against simple scratches and abrasions for daily use. I was hoping for a little shock and water protection, which this case minimally provides.

The appearance is nice. It does add a little bulk to the camera but still allows you to handle all the controls. The rubber is grippy which makes holding it a little more secure but at the price that it also clings to any dust it comes in contact with. I do like the clear plastic protective screen. The lens cover seems a little pointless. The one use I have found for it, is to use to block out light when shooting through glass at zoos and aquariums, but even for that it is of limited value.

Pros
+ Good added protections from scrapes and scratches
+ Clear Plastic
+ Add's a Grippieness to the camera

Cons
- Gathers dust
- MSRP is rather high for the payoff
- Adds a little bulk

Summary:
This product is ok at protecting the aesthetics of your camera for resale for sure. I'm a little dubious about any shock protection during a drop, but I feel it is worth having installed. It does not get in the way of functionality. Probably not worth full MSRP, but does have value.

I like this case. It is just a simple, snug fitting, rubber armored feeling case. It doesn't have man whistles and bells, although I am happy they threw in a bonus screen protector and cleaning cloth. I wasn't looking for much, just a little more protection for our iPod 5th Gen. It does seem like it will help kid proof it in several ways. First, the rubbery finish is grippy and makes it a little harder to have it slip from your fingers. Also it protects the camera bump that has always seemed a little exposed, I am glad that it now seems recessed.

I like the classy smoky gray look although it kind of takes away from the fact that the blue back was specially chosen, but I'll take the scratch protection over being able to see the blue. Also, I like the thinness of the iPod and this case doesn't add that much bulk

I'm giving it 4 stars because it is pretty basic and doesn't blow me out of the water, but I am very happy with it. I would recommend it for a simple scratch resistant cover.

I bought a [[ASIN:B00542NV32 Garmin eTrex 10 Worldwide Handheld GPS Navigator]] a while ago and and was fairly happy with it except that I have two boys and there was some squabbling over who got to hold the GPS. I figured that a second GPS would solve the problem (which it did, except I still don't have one.)

This is a still a pretty basic GPS unit, but very usable for us small time geocachers. The embedded maps on this device are far better than the Garmin and I like the overall design better. Otherwise the functionality is pretty much the same, right down to the less than intuitive menus and lack of an easy way to simply input a coordinate. If you are trying to set a waypoint or mark a location, it is very straight forward. Likewise, downloading geocache coordinates is great. However, I have yet to find a great way to input a coordinate. Why isn't there an option of a "Go to this coordinate" button that then prompts you to enter the coordinate? That seems completely intuitive to me, yet I cannot find this functionality on either this or the etrex. (please comment if you know how to do this, I have just been altering existing waypoints or caches.)

I don't think I could be happier with the form factor. It fits well in the hand and is, for lack of a better word, cute. I have had fun using this with the boys and I appreciate another excuse to get them outside and almost unwired for a while. I have also used it to mark fishing spots on lakes and keep general information for walks. It's a very nice little unit.

I have been using this device for quite a while now and I have enjoyed having it as a network storage device. Perhaps the best thing I can say about it is that it has been working quietly and steadily, acting as a file server and back up to my older Mac Laptop. I have never had to recover from the backup, but I like the security of having the back up (I have verified files are backed up.) The device is quiet and has needed no real interaction from me.

When I first got the device I was wowed by all the possibilities, but I have not actually used any of the whistles and bells, just the raw disk space. So I can't really say much about that, but I will say that it has been a great and dependable product for me.

I love this device. It has performed loyally every day for over a year and fills my appartment with crisp and satisfying sound. While I could find it, the remote worked flawlessly to control but a click wheel and touch ipod. The only glitch I have ever seen is that occassionaly the sound will stop when there is any kind of hiccup in the wiring - like an air-conditioner kicking in.

I have used the accompanying software for my alarm clock for 6 months now and love it except that it keeps the screen of the iPod Touch lit so there is extra light in the room. But the church bells are an effective and pleasing way to wake up.

I guess I can't say too much about this dock though. It kind of just works. It has been dependable.

Good Points

- Good Sound
- Dependable performance
- Fully compatible with my iPods
- Nice looking

Bad Points

- Distortion at moderately high levels (but not at comfortable levels)
- remote apparently hard to refind.

I recommend this device to anyone looking for a classy looking shelf dock for their iPod.

I have been using this sling for some time now. When I received this sling I was seriously looking at buying the [[ASIN:B0036AWR8E Lowepro SlingShot 202 AW]] and I think for my purposes, this is the better sling for me. The one thing I did not like about the Lowpro was that it was broken up into two compartments which limited my ability to put my Canon 200-400 5.6 zoom in it comfortably. The large main compartment easily, but snugly holds my 40D and lense, which room to spare to include a wide angle.

As for slings in general. I have a Tamarac backpack which I love, but tend to way over pack (because I can.) It is bulky and awkward to wear, but does have a hip belt to take the weight off the shoulders. Also, I tried a holster style case, but it never felt secure and I never trusted my camera and lense in such a flimsy case. The sling, once in place seems to become a part of my body while hiking and climbing. It feels more secure than the backpack and far more secure than the holster.

Good Points

- nice spacious compartment for a DSLR and Zoom lense
- Sturdy with strap across you chest, it feels very secure on.
- Rotating the sling gives a sturdy platform to remove or insert camera.
- It is not big enough to overpack
- plenty of space for battery, charger, cards, notebook or guide, and two lenses and body
- Rain cover is nice addition (have not used it, but love the extra insurance.)
- Well padded
- Nice construction, classic design.
- Nice side handle for carrying when not slung.

Bad Points

- Sling Accentuates Man-boobs (I've tried several different ways of placing the strap, but it seems the only fix is portion control and moderate exercise.)
- no hip belt so weight is held on shoulders for long hikes, but weight is limited somewhat by size.

All in all, I have to admit I have come to love this sling. It has traveled with me quite a bit and I trust it to hold my treasured camera and lense. Easy to pack and will handle the essentials. It is cheaper than the Lowe sling in price, but not functionality. I recommend this to anyone who wants to pack in a DSLR.

I don't think I asked a lot in a iPad cover, but I'm impressed how well this cover has delivered. Mostly I was looking for functional protection and a look that classy looks. This cover delivered both in spades.

Protection:

I love the way the iPad is held in place by the four rubber corner holder. The case makes contact with the iPad in the most minimal way and does not allow grit to get between the case and the ipad to scratch surfaces. I have never had the iPad slip out of these feet either, it is very snugly held in place.

The outside materials are rugged and there are 3/16th inches of touch material between the iPad and the harsh world. It will not protect it in a long fall, but it is safe from scratches and smudges.

Looks:

I was originally looking for a leather case for looks, but this is just as classy as the leather cases I have found for twice the price. I like the leatherlike surface and the black with white stitching is subtly striking. I even like the Belkin logo, it's a cute representation of the human form.

Functionality:

The magnet is well placed to hold the case closed, then when open, it holds the front flap securely attached to the back of the iPad. Magnet strength seems to be strong enough to be functional. Also well designed are the multiple positions the case folds into. It has a great adjustable angle fold for watching movies and using my bluetooth keyboard.

I don't use the camera ever, but this case does have a strategically placed hole so it is available.

Failings:

In general this is a great case. The two things I can think of for constructive criticism are the inside materials and the fact that the magnet causes the iPad to wake in transit. For the inside material, it is a velvety black material that picks up dust. Not a huge thing, but noticeable. As for the magnet, I guess this is not uncommon, but I do completely power down the iPad if I am putting it in my laptop bag. Otherwise it occassionally turns on and runs down the battery. Again not a bad thing and not an issue in general.

Summary:

All in all, I love this case. It's classy and functional. Recommend.

Out of the box, this is a stunning piece of electronics. The screen size is impressive as is the simplicity of the unit itself. Turning it on it continued to be impressive. I charged it the required time and turned it on and it just kept on impressing.

However as I use it more and more, I find issues with the interface and unfortunately the car power adapter. The first thing to end the honeymoon with this device was the fact that it kept telling me I was speeding. Easy enough, I'll turn that off. I navigated to the settings and turned this feature off. But, at this point there was no submit option, just back. So I could change the setting but never submit the change. This frustrated me and my human navigator till we turned it off. Later we found that we could turn it off, but not during it's active navigation.

Otherwise it is very feature rich. I am impressed how easily I can find any address in the state and beyond. The turn by turn works well and it has helped me find several homes and businesses I was unfamiliar with.

But about 6 weeks into using the device it blipped off and would not restart. It took some troubleshooting but I tracked it down to the power cord. It will still charge with the AC adapter but the car adapter cord is shot. This severely limits the functionality of the device since the on board battery last barely 30 minutes. I have been reduced to using an AC inverter to get it to work on longer trips. The cable not working is a major bummer, but better than when I thought the entire unit fried.

But all in all I do like the basic functionality of the GPS. I don't know that I can go without a turn by turn GPS from here on out.

OK, I guess one more beef I have to give. I, like 10% of all males, have partial color blindness, and the green from the proper road is very hard to distiguish from the beige of the other roads. I am told that it is pretty clear to others, but a little trickier for me.

I have to confess I am not an audiophile but Sennheiser is starting to change that. A year ago I got [[ASIN:B002YOENAS Sennheiser PXC 310 BT Compact Noise-Canceling Travel Headphones with Bluetooth Technology (Black)]] and I have fallen in love with them. When I got a chance to get a review pair for MM 450's I jumped. These are ever bit as good as old ones and I can't wait to use them on a flight soon.

--Use: It is very easy to pair these to blue tooth devices. I mostly use these in conjunction with an iPod Touch. In the evening I usually switch from speakers to headphones so as not to annoy the neighbors and the headphones take over immediately when I turn them on. Also I enjoy being able to skip forward and backward in the playlists by tapping the buttons on the ear piece. I still have issues with missed phone calls, but I get absolutely no distractions when working with them on (short of a fire alarm.)

--Sound: The Sennheiser sound is better than any headphones I have ever had. I'm not a big fan of base and at first I felt that they did not get loud enough, but now I appreciate that I cranked my headphones to get over room noise. With the noise canceling this is not an issue.

--Design: I love the folding design. they fold flat and fairly narrow and fit into its well designed carrying case well. The smaller ear muffs are not as hot as the full sized ones which is nice and fit comfortably on the head, although sometimes I feel a little twist due to the folding hinges. But all in all they are well crafted and comfortable.

Pros
--Great Sound
--Great Remote controls for my iPod
--A usable and classy carrying case for cables/headphones
--Extreme ease of use
--Hard-wired cable works great
--Long lasting batter - rarely need to recharge
--Amazing folding design makes it fit into my computer bag very well

Cons
--I find little point to the talk through option
--Sometimes noise canceling cuts you off from the world a little too much
--Hard-wired cable seems proprietary so I'm afraid to lose it
--Makes it hard to live with cheaper headphones

I'm still not an audiophile, but Sennheiser has made it impossible for me to go back to my old cheap headphones. You do get what you pay for, and these are worth the price.

I had never used a lens pen before so I did a little research on you tube and I'm not sure how I got along without one. It's one of those things you don't need every day, but when you do need it, it is wonderful to have. The pen shaped design makes it ultimately portable and fits into any camera bag or vest. The retractable brush is fantastic and the part that I thought I would use the most. It did everything I hoped for in removing dust from optics.

What surprised me, due to ignorance is the fiber pads opposite of the brush. I had not used it, and initially was pretty leery of it. The reversible pad stem with the round and triangular pads are fantastic. Like I said I was leery, so initially I only used it to clean the viewfinder on my dslr's and my binoculars. The triangular pad easily got years of gunk out of the tightest corners of the viewfinder and the circular pad works great on the bins.

It took a video to fully understand that there was carbon in the pen cap and that you twist it to reprime the pads and clean them. If I had one bit of constructive criticism it would be lack of even the barest instructions in the box. Turned out there was more than met the eye for me. Also, a little overpackaged for something the size of a pen.

But, all in all, this is a great, solid, functional tool. I really don't know why I didn't get one years ago.

I'm pretty happy with these headphones, I received a reviewer pair intending to use them as my work headphones, and hope to make use of the sound canceling capabilities. My previous head phones are [[ASIN:B002YOENAS Sennheiser PXC 310 BT Compact Noise-Canceling Travel Headphones with Bluetooth Technology (Black)]] so that is what I am comparing them to.

Sound---

I am very happy with the clarity of the sound from these headphones. The music is crisp and has decent highs and lows. The one thing I am a little disappointed with is there seems to be a lot of distortion when turned to just a moderately high volume. Which probably works well with my use at work, but I can't truly crank these headphones without getting too much distortion. Of course this is probably good for my hearing, but to continue the comparison to the Sennheisers, these have less capability at higher volumes.

When listening to these at lower volume though, they are very nice. I'm not a huge audiophile, but I can appreciate the sound quality these deliver.

Sound canceling appears to work fairly well. I can at least attest to the fact that I missed phone calls while listening to these, I am interested to see how the will work to cut airplane noise.

Design ---

I'm impressed with the way these headphones have been designed to fold for storage and transport. They are not as compact as my Sennheisers, but they do fold into a decent size and the nice leatherette case holds them well, with space to spare for extra accessories. The ear pieces swivel well to form to you head, the cable connects firmly and securely, and the battery compartment is well designed.

Also, I am impressed that they thought to add an adapter for an airline headphone jack. I am looking forward to having these to listen to on my next air trip.

Comfort---

The ear pieces are nicely padded that make a nice comfortable fit. I have historically only used ear buds so at times my ears seem to get warm due to the coverage of the ear pieces. The bar is padded but noticeable on your head, again for those used to earbuds this takes an adjustment.

Summary---

All in all these are nice headphones. I prefer my Sennheisers which do deliver a little better sound on the corded connection (less sound quality over Bluetooth.) However, I am happy with these, but not enough to justify the price savings over the Sennheisers.

I was a little disappointed with these headphones. Perhaps I got a slightly defective set as the sound is very noticeably better with my [[ASIN:B002SSO06M Sennheiser PXC 310 Compact Noise-Canceling Travel Headphones (Black)]]. There is a bit of buzz in the sound and they seem to distort at moderately high levels.

Also, the blue tooth connectivity seems weaker than my PCX 310's. I get a lot of dropouts and 15 foot range from my laptop. I have found that I only use these patched into my work computer with the included cord. I have not been overly impressed with the bluetooth sound quality on these headphones, but they are pretty sleek and comfortable. The bluetooth set up and quick and easy and I have no troubles getting connected to my laptop. I just have issues when I move away from my laptop.

Corded, the sound is fairly good, but does not live up to the sticker price. For $300 dollars I expect stellar sound quality and I'm not getting that from these.

----- Updated with an apology to Sennheiser ------

It turned out that the muddy sound I was getting from these headphones were from my laptop, not from the headphones. I have since gotten a new iPod Touch as well as used them on a high end stereo system. The Bluetooth is friggin awesome. With my iPod on a dock I can use these throughout my entire apartment including lobby with no drops or distortion.

I apologize to Sennheiser for mistakenly blaming the headphones. Here is the original review, unchanged. Please note that any notes about the bluetooth quality is in error. I have also raised my review to the full five stars it deserves, 9 months later and I love these headphones.

----------------------------------------------------

I was very happy to receive a reviewer pair of these head phones. They promise a great audio experience and for the most part they truly deliver. I have recently moved into a very quiet apartment complex and was looking forward to being able to continue cranking my music while not disturbing my neighbors.

I was impressed unboxing the headphones. These headphones are nicely engineered and I listened to them hardwired while charging the batteries, I was very happy with the sound quality. The fit and comfort were nice, but a little warm and confining when compared to ear buds. But, I lost a little love when using the bluetooth option. The bluetooth set up was easy enough, but it was a little muddy when connected to my laptop. Also the range was about 15 feet, and only line of sight so I could not leave the room without skips and dropouts.

The only other word of critique I have for them is that their noise canceling is a little too effective. I find myself missing phone calls when just 10 feet from the ringing phone. These are very nice headphones when listening with the included headphone cable, but don't live up to their bluetooth promise for me. I don't know if I would be very impressed for the price. They are nice, but perhaps not $300 nice.

OK I admit it, I am leery of Linksys wireless routers. I have had four routers in my life (the E4200 being the fifth) and only the Linksys router gave me headaches. I vowed to never get another Linksys in my life, but I like Cisco so this was a dilemna and so far I am have been happy with it.

Design

This is a very slick device. I love the low profile that lets it hide on top of the cabinet it is on. A nice looking piece of hardware.

Setup

I have never had an easier set up on any wireless router. I installed the software onto my MacBook (mac friendly) and it self-discovered and prompted for the rest of the set up. Very nice setup, although a little long from beginning to end (7 minutes or so.) I loved that it prompted to personalize the SSID and password right up front. Software was slick and straight forward. Once set up I had all 7 wireless devices in the house on-line in about 20 minutes. Even my wireless printer worked instantly. - Five stars on Set-up

Functionality

I have only had the device installed for a weekend now, but I spent that time backing up my hard drive to a wireless SAN, watching streaming netflix and uploading a new website. No hiccups at all. About the only thing I did have an issue with is trying to set it up with my Ooma. I needed to rebooted the router and modem after removing the Ooma. No blame here, the Ooma doesn't seem to want to play nicely with any router or cable modem.

I really like the ability to have a guest network. It is easily turned off and on so I can easily provide a connection to visitors, but turn it off and totally deny the Brazilian students next door (actually it is password protected so it is not wide open, but less secure.)

Speed

I may not be the best to judge speed. I am not the type to watch the throughput numbers, but I can say that netflix streamed Mars Attacks wirelessly to my Wii without any issues. I have no issues with the speed at all.

Conclusion

I am very happy with the router. Who knows, two years down the line, I may be able to let my prejudice against Linksys go. If things continue to go well, or if they take a turn for the worse, I will update this review.

To let you know where I am coming from on this review, I have two sons, 9 and 4. We do a lot of camping without mom, but want to share our adventures. So far, our trips have destroyed a Canon Powershot 450 (overly hydrated while canoeing) and a Powershot 980IS (smashed into ground during a fall.) So the idea of a waterproof, shockproof and hopefully kid-proof camera sounded perfect.

Purpose for camera: Rugged camera to take along canoeing, fishing, camping, and hiking for snapshots and quick, shareable movies.

I have never owned a camera in this class, and the one thing I am trying to keep in mind is the price point. This is not intended to be a high-end performance device, but more a rugged snapshot camera. I was a little suspect on 1080P on a hand held device under $175 (still am,) but the 5 MP camera is adequate for photos to email to grandparents and to show off our catches and camps to mom.

Design -

The camera is very nicely designed. It is physically attractive and comfortable in the hand. The winged doors lock into place well in their watertight positions and are, well kind of cool. The screen is adequate for playback and we spend a lot of time watching what we filmed over and over. The controls are spare, but easy to understand and operate. The four major flaws I found are; the embedded battery, lack of a flash, lack of lens cover, and no headphone jack for previewing sound.

Battery-

It is unfortunate that the design team decided to go with an internal non-removable battery. This seems to move the device into the "disposable" class since it is useless once the battery dies. I suspect that the battery can be replaced fairly easily, judging by the hex screws in the camera body, but there is a big difference between slipping a battery in and out and sending the camera out for replacement. Also, I can make a huge argument for being able to carry a back up battery. At least for now though, the battery seems to have a decent charge. We have filmed and played back films for at least two hours between recharges and have never seen the battery near empty.

Performance -

Image capture: 1080p is a lot to ask from such a small sensor. For that matter, so is 720p. So I am satisfied with the images I am getting, not great but what I would expect. I usually shoot Canon DSLR's (except when camping with kids) so I am at times frustrated by the lack of manual controls of any kind. Autofocus, autoexposure... with no way to change anything beyond file format and resolution. The images and video I am getting are a little noisy and especially so in low light. Blurring from camera or subject motion is common on stills. This is where the flash option would be nice. But in daylight, or decently lit interior shots the images are definitely passable. Again, judging this camera on its price point and function, it really is decent. If I want good stills, I'll go with a Canon 50D, if I want a snapshot of my kid pulling a bass into the canoe, this is perfect.

I am uploading a video with more details on picture and movie quality.

Sound: For a single source mike on the camera, it does pretty good. Definitely picks up footsteps or breathing, so don't film while walking up hill. Truly emphasizes if you are out of shape. Picks up ambient sound well and in tests in a light breeze, did fine.

Interface: I had the interface lock up on me once and I was unable to get it to power off or get out of a locked state. I had to use the small reset button to get it to reboot and clear the freeze. So I have thrown a very small paper clip in its case. Without being able to pull the battery, the reset button seems to have been the only option. Otherwise the device is very fast loading up, and the interface is intuitive and easy to use. Although occasionally when browsing I end up in fast forward or reverse when watching a movie and it takes a little to get it back to play or browse.

Summary:

All in all, I am really happy with this camera. It is full of limitations which you should understand before purchase. For the price, it is a decent camera and it fits our intended purpose to a Tee. My kids love the ability to take a movie, then watch it immediately. I like the feeling that it might survive the kids for a while. I feel like I'm being pretty critical of the camera, and I guess I am. But I'm giving it four stars because it does what I want it to, and after using it for a couple weeks, I really like it. Just don't expect the world from a inexpensive camera.

Pros-
Price (under $175 is not a high end price)
Images are decent (under daylight or bright light conditions)
Kidproof
Quick to startup
Well thought-out design
Just all round cute and useful

Cons (in order of importance to me)
Internal Battery (cannot be replaced, nor can you carry a spare)
No Flash (can't stop motion blur, fill flash)
Low-light performance (weak performance, noisy video and stills)
Complete lack of manual controls
Occasional lock-ups on interface
No Head phones for reviewing movies
When switching through modes it keeps defaulting to zoomed out

First - What I was looking for

My wife has been working on a series of juvenile fiction books over her summer breaks. Much of that time has been spent at the municipal pool for kids' swim lessons or open swims. So we were looking for a waterproof, functional cover for her iPad (I know, who writes books on an iPad, but she is an adept hunt and peck typer and it works well for her.)

What we got

As for protection and performance, we got exactly what we were looking for. It is not waterproof, but it is secure enough for the potential poolside splashing and dripping. The double zip-locks form strong secure seals. The screen works well for her typing and allowed her to have all the functionality she was looking for. At least for the poolside purposes.

What wasn't quite up to our hopes.

It is not exactly easy to slip the iPad in and out of this case. Personally I think it borders on being enough hassle that it may make her decide not to use it in the long run. Also the iPad needs to be removed for charging or access to the headphone port etc. Obviously this is needed for water-proofing, but this does make it less likely to be used.

Also we had a small issue when we left the cover in the car at below freezing temperatures then brought it in. I did not let it warm before trying to open the seals and one of the seal rails cracked. It still makes a good seal, but should not be opened or closed at freezing temperatures.

Summary

While not perfect, it should be perfect for our needs. Construction is good (see note on sub zero temperatures)and functionality is good. All in all happy with it.

This is not a particularly loud sound system, but it does fill our small bedroom adequately to a reasonable volume. It will not fill a large room or outdoor area for sure, or belt out heavy metal, but does great at an adult contemporary listening level.

After getting this, one thing became quickly evident. The lack of a remote kind of sucks. This doesn't seem like a big idea, and for the price, it is understandable that there is no remote, but I found that it is worth the extra money to get a speaker system with a remote.

One thing I really like about it is the portability and the ability to run off of batteries. We have used it a couple times at night to play owl calls to hear owls call back to us. Also, since it is so portable we move it all around the house and garage which is very handy.

However after using them for a day, one speaker stopped working. I could sync it with the base station, but no sound would come out.

I called the 1-800 customer line which is a recording requesting me to call a non-800 long distance line. Feeling a little Baited and Switched, I called the number and spoke to a nice enough representative who said to just return the item to Amazon. There was no RMA option to work directly with the manufacturer. So I was not impressed with their Customer Service.

Since this was a Amazon Vine reviewer item, no one at Amazon knew anything about how to return the device. So I was not feeling too satisfied with the quality of the product and had no way to return it for exchange. So I took a close look and noticed that the front power light was off centered, so using a little Newtonian Physics and the base of my hand I gave it a firm whack on the side. The sound started immediately. It's needed a couple more whacks, but it seems to be in line now.

So, all in all, I am happy except that the ipod tray seems a little cheap, It uses up the power of three separate devices rather than one, and their customer service left me high and dry. But the sound is pretty good and it fills my workshop well. But bear in mind, this was a free reviewer item. If I had to pay for this, received a poorly constructed item and such limited customer service, I would not have been very satisfied.

My wife, like many women, is obsessed with organization. When she saw the collapsible trunk box that came with our Mini Clubman she needed one for the Jeep. So when I got a chance to get Thule Trunk Organizer from Amazon Vine I jumped at it.

I have long been familiar with Thule for their car racking products, so I knew this organizer would not be cheap, neither in construction or price. And this organizer falls right in with the rest of their product line; it is ruggedly constructed, carefully designed, and a little over-priced. This is a quality product but the 39.99 list price seems a little steep for what is essentially a twenty-first century basket.

Collapsed, the organizer is just a fraction of an inch tall, almost flush with the floor. Once the supporting wire side supports are in place the frame forms a sturdy and rigid basket. My wife found the process of popping it up to be a little less than obvious, but it is pretty straightforward. It does take a little muscling to set the side wires but this also insures that it does not collapse accidentally or at a mere jostling. Once set up, and the wires pushed into their proper place, the organizer is very sturdy.

I was a little worried about ordering it without a clear idea of its size. 41 Liters is a little less than a 10 gallon aquarium which at least gave me a ballpark idea. To make it a little easier to visualize, I posted a photo with a milk carton and grocery bag.

I do wish there was some way to give it a shoulder strap. It can carry quite a bit, but due to the design that puts a handle on each side, it must be carried with two hands. So, if you have it filled with groceries, it will need it's own dedicated trip from the car to the kitchen. It would be nice if there were a way to carry it with one hand.

Pros
Rugged Construction
Quality Materials
Thoughtful, functional design
Collapsed size is very small
Attractive

Cons
A little pricey
No shoulder or one handed way to carry.

Overall, a great and flexible organizer for a trunk or cargo area.

My first question was "What is 802.11ac?" - In December 2011 "802.11ac" was the next evolution of WiFi & enabled wireless speeds over a gigabit per second.

"b" was the first there was (802.11b) which provided up to 11 mbps data rates per radio in the 2.4 GHz spectrum.
"a" was the next evolution (802.11a) which provided up to 54 mbps data rates per radio in the 5 GHz spectrum.
"g"came out shortly after enabling 54 mbps per radio in the 2.4 GHz spectrum.
"n" was ratified in 2009 (802.11n) allows for data rates up to 600 mbps per radio.
"ac" builds on 802.11n.

setup took 2 minutes; I plugged the TP Extender into a wall plug outside the room the router was in. Wait until the `power' and `wi-fi' LEDs light up; then press the WPS button on the router (this is the reason it isn't going to work at a motel/hotel). Then I pressed the Range Extender button on the TP Extender the lowest on the front of the device (must do it within 2 minutes). The LED on the TP Extender should go from flashing to solid, showing that WPS connection has succeeded. Done.

tips:

there are 6 lights on the TP Extender the top two should be green, if they are RED your extender is too far from the router. If it is no color it means you need to reconnect the router and the extender by repeating the steps above.

> to minimize wireless interference keep the Range Extender away from cordless phones, Bluetooth devices and Microwave Ovens.

> If possible place the TP Extender in open corridors or spacious locations rather than a crowded room.

Frankly I have not noticed any difference in our wi-fi but we have a smaller home (1700 sq feet) the router we have is 2 years old and is in one room in the house while I use my 3 year old laptop (Sony Viao series E) in the livingroom 2 rooms away and 2 walls away. I do plan on bringing it with us on vacation where I am hoping that where we do get poor reception (where we have access to a router), we will get a noticeable improvement.

The device has a reset option (if the TP Extender doesn't seem to be working): While the Range Extender is plugged into a power outlet, press the RESET button (located next to the ethernet port underneath the TP Extender) with a pen for 1 second. Wait 2 seconds until all the LEDs flash once.

*Bonus - The Range Extender's ETHERNET port allows it to function as a wireless adapter for a wired devices (Blu-ray players, game consoles, DVRs and smart TVs) allowing the device to share the wireless network.

If you use this adapter on anything with vibration, do NOT buy this adapter, you will regret it. The other Fotodiox adapters are much better than quality than this adapter.
Very nice quality product to hide the wires up behind the TV.

Great charger! My batteries take 8-10 hours to charge in my flashlight, but if I take them out and use the smart charger, they are good to go in way less than half that time. I like the quality and performance of this unit and I would definitely recommend it.

Awesome little product! I have an expensive smoker but I still use one or two of these smoker tubes. I have the 12" for quick cooks - 2 hours or less and the 18" for 6 hours or less. I use both when I want real extreme smoking! The trick is to fill the smoker tube with pellets and use a little torch with map gas to light the pellets, wait at least 5 minutes and blow out the flame and set in the smoker or barbeque. Remember to set the tube on some aluminum foil because the ashes will fall through the grates and make a mess. Note: if you light both ends of the tube, you get double the smoke but half of the time before it goes out. I have bought several of these for gifts for friends with smokers and they all say great things about this product.

Update: I have a RecTec smoker and I use their wood pellets because the burn so clean as compared to my old Traeger with Traiger pellets. I tried using the RecTec pellets in my smoke tube this past weekend and I didn't get as large of volume of smoke but they burned a lot longer than the Traeger pellets. I switched back to the cheaper Traeger pellets for my smoke tube because I like the larger volume of smoke and because I set the smoke tube on some aluminum foil, I don't get all of the ash in my smoker.
Nice quality cable like the cable that came with my Mophie battery case. I was happy with the quality of the product.
I purchased this for my Dell powered speakers. The adapter worked just the original adapter, so I have no complaints.
Great quality, not much else to say..... I am sold on Mediabridge products, I'll never shop around again for cables - you will to if you try them!

Simple; plug it in and use it. The new traffic receiver took about 10 minutes to display the local traffic information the first time but after that, it worked just like my original traffic receiver. The new traffic receiver arrived quickly just as all of my Amazon orders do!

I like these head phones when I want to sleep with music. The only down side is that there is a cord which has been wrapped around my neck once or twice. I am now getting better at pulling them off before I completely doze off. These headphones are a nice quality product.
Cable Matters make quality cables. I usually buy Mediabridge cables but I would not hesitate to purchase other cables I need from this manufacturer. You will not be disappointed.

These cables were way beyond what I expected to receive. The quality is excellent and connections are tight.
I will only buy Mediabridge cables in the future!
I had this since November 2021 and by March 2022 it was suddenly jumping around the screen and the refusing to track. It has no damage or water spills or anything like that. Just gone.

I really like this case. It looks like an actual composition book except for the folding grooves on the cover. It holds an Apple Pencil and has a nice little round slot for temporary storage of the Apple Pencil cap while you’re charging it. The groove for holding the Apple Pencil is flexible so not too difficult to pull the pencil out. Also has some additional room in the pencil slot to store the pencil’s little power adapter. The iPad fits snugly and securely. The folding cover works excellently as a stand and the cover does perform the auto-off on the iPad when closing. One of the best covers I’ve ever owned.

I have to say I'm pretty impressed with how the TCL "The Creative Life" 40-inch 1080P 60Hz LCD HDTV is working for us. We've plugged in our laptops and we're streaming video on a "high-speed" DSL connection. Simple as plug and play. No missing pixels, straight-forward setup. I can't think of one bad or neutral thing to say about this screen. Great TV for the bedroom if you have the space, or for a small living room. Quality of picture is great.

I was a bit hesitant to buy this because it seemed like it was targeted towards smaller Mac books and I have an HP Envy x360 and it's on the bigger side of the suggested size. Thankfully it fits just right and is cushioned nicely inside. It's such a cute color and has good pockets on it too!
Works great! Love it!
AWESOME! Been using for a couple months now with no problems!
Love. I only wish I had more time to spend on it--it's addicting and sooo good with graphic artistry! LOVE.
LOVE! High quality and adorable!
This adapter allows me to connect my iPad pro to older TVs and monitors via HDMI cable. I bought one for each of my screens that doesn't have AirPlay. Picture & sound are clear.
Works well with my ipad. Was perfect for sharing a screen in a public space.
Perfect adapter to connect my ThinkPad Yoga to an old style monitor. Takes up virtually no desk space.

Great sound. Connects easily to my ipad. No sound delay - lip movements match voices when watching movies or tv shows. Have not used with a phone, but the pause/play button is convenient for use with my ipad. I liked this enough to buy another one for use with my ThinkPad Yoga.

I'm on my third one of these. I can't live without one. Protects the screen well, but I still put the keyboard & ipad into a Built sleeve to provide some padding for both items. Holds a charge for a long time. Long enough that it takes me a bit to realize that it would work better if I'd give it a bit of electric juice. I don't advise actual liquids though. I doused my first two with glasses of water, immediately dried them off and stuffed into a bag of rice. Each would still connect to my ipad after water damage, but typing resulted in gobbledygook. Best to keep it dry.

These are great iPad stands. I tried one and ended up buying 3 more for various spots around my home. I used them with my naked iPad for months. They take up very little space and are lightweight for travel. I recently covered my iPad with a case that covers the back and edges and the combined unit still fits in these stands. Highly recommend.

Here's the name of the iPad case that I purchased from Amazon a few weeks ago:

iPad 2 Case,iPad 3 Case,iPad 4 Case,Agrigle 2 in 1 Light Weight Shockproof Hybrid Defender Rugged Protection Cover Case with Kickstand For iPad 2/3/4 (Kickstand-Black)

Wonderful travel surge protector. The green light that lets the user know the device is protecting from surges is quite bright. Works well as a nightlight if you need one. I recommend covering the light with electrical tape if you like your hotel room or bedroom dark at night. I use mine in the kitchen when I'm not on the road.

This TV was a gift from our 3 kids at Christmas, and seems to be a good TV. That being said, for someone like me and my husband, who are “old school”, there is a learning curve in using this w/o jumping feet first into all of the “smart” technology. We are having to use 2 controllers to use it (sure there’s a better way), but we haven’t figured it out. Helps immensely. Just follow the directions on the you tube video.

I have a mid-range gaming laptop that I have converted over to Linux for the purpose of virtualization testing, software development and media. It has a built-in HDMI port on the embedded video adapter but it has a known chipset issue with HDMI output and is basically unusable. I looked to this adapter to handle converting between USB-C to HDMI to work around that problem. It has worked out perfectly, with no glitches or problems whatsoever, at a really nice price point.

The adapter is very simple and straightforward. It plugs into a USB-C port on one end and it accepts an HDMI connection on the other. There’s no switch, no software to install or configure, no weird settings that need to be found in the OS to make this thing work – just plug it in. I plugged it into my laptop with the monitor connected and the system immediately recognized the display, identified the make and model, and set up my desktop for me. The only configuration I needed to do was in the Linux desktop (KDE Plasma), and it gave me the options for setting the default behavior. My external monitor runs at full resolution too, and so far I have not seen any lag (though to be fair, I do not game on this system so I really am not pushing it).

The price is very reasonable considering how well it works. As I write this the adapter is selling for $10.99 (subject to change, I am sure), and it’s worth every bit of that price.

This adapter has met a need I had with my system and I am very pleased. It’s a very simple device for a specific purpose, and if you need such an adapter it’s a very good choice. Based on my experience with it, it’s very easy to give it a hearty recommend.

I recently purchased a new zoom lens for my camera after I broke the old one when I took a tumble. I had filters like these for my old lens but the thread size was different so my old filters were no longer useful. I selected this filter for my new lens, somewhat apprehensively because of the relatively low asking price. It has proven to be a decent filter but it is not useful in all situations.

The idea behind this filter is light diffusion which will give an image a very slight haze or softness, depending on the lighting and subject. This is an effect that can be emulated in software during post-processing but in doing this type of enhancement I have found it is sometimes unnatural. It certainly is less fun than making it happen while shooting, which is why these types of filters are available.

In use it works, though I have had mixed results. When using it with certain light sources, the filter seems to have no real effect at all, while with others it creates a subtle, soft glow around the subject. I am still working out the situations where it is most effective. I have had similar issues with filters like these with other lenses, and as such I assume the problem is in my lack of practice with them. It will take some time and practice to make my results more consistent, and for now I lay the fault on myself.

The build quality seems to be good. I have received filters in the past where the glass rattles in the frame which is unsettling. This one is tight and there is no play between the glass and the frame. It screws on to the lens securely and is easy to clean.

The asking price is quite reasonable. I have seen these filters priced much higher, and I have also seen much cheaper ones that do not work well. The pricing seems in line with the product, if not slightly low.

I have no complaints with this filter. The issues I have with it are probably my inexperience, and I will keep working with it to improve my results. I will return here and update my review if my impression changes. For now, though, I am satisfied.

I selected this hub/docking station for a new laptop that did not come with an SD card reader, a tool I used almost daily with my older system. As I looked for options and features I began to realize that I can use extra ports and interfaces too, though the card reader was the main consideration. After doing a good bit of research I settled on this hub and I am very pleased with it so far.

This is a small device, about the size of a deck of playing cards. It’s shelled in an aluminum casing so it is durable enough to handle getting battered around my desk a little which is a good thing. It comes with a USB-C cable, but I have not used the included cable, opting instead to use a cable that is able to handle higher wattage and was purchased at the same time; I’ll keep the included cable as a spare.

I had no issues with connection and my Windows 11 system was able to see it and set it up automatically with no manual effort at all. It quite literally has been plug and play for me.

The card reader works flawlessly for me. I have used it with two different cards and the system sees the cards as soon as they’re inserted into the reader.

I have not tried all of the other interfaces this device offers, but I did plug an external USB drive into the hub and it worked exactly as if it was plugged into one of the onboard ports. Speeds are excellent and I have had no problems with time-outs or stalls when moving large amounts of data across the interface.

What I have not tried yet, because I haven’t had the time, is connecting to my Linux system. My Linux system has an odd issue with the HDMI port (a known hardware issue with the graphics card model), and I want to see how well this hub addresses the conversion from USB-C to HDMI. If this solves the issue with that system’s HDMI connectivity when I try it, I’ll be buying another one. Once I have tried this I will update my review. If it doesn’t work with Linux it’s okay – the product description does not mention Linux as a supported platform, so if it does happen to work it’s a bonus.

My experience with this hub/dock has been very positive and for me it has been worth the expense. It’s expensive when considering I just needed an external card reader, but when considering everything else it does it’s a good investment for my system.

A UV filter on a lens can be a cheap and effective way to protect your expensive glass. Some of these filters are better than others, and this one is on the lower end of the scale. That said, it's worth its asking price.

Most digital cameras already have decent UV filtering built in so there's not a lot of sense to getting a UV filter for that purpose. However, these filters do have a very important role - they provide very inexpensive protection for the lens, for both dirt and scratches. An inexpensive filter like this is a lot less expensive to replace than a lens that cost hundreds of dollars.

My complaint with this filter is the same as with other inexpensive filters I have used. It's reflective, and in certain situations I can get reflections between the lens and the filter that can mess up an otherwise good image. A fine example is when photographing trains or oncoming cars that have turned on their headlamps. In those cases, this filter interferes and causes very noticeable reflections when the angle is just right.

The majority of the time, this filter is fine protection for my lens and I shoot with it in place. However, there are times when it is a detriment and I remove it for those cases. A more expensive filter that cuts down reflections is a better choice for those situations. However, those filters cost a lot more in most cases.

This is a decent UV filter for the price. It provides good basic protection for the lens on which it is attached and the price is reasonable. There are cases where it's more of a problem than a help, though, and for those cases it is easy enough to remove.

I have a gold streak filter that I use occasionally with my main lens. This is the first blue streak filter I have used and I use it with my most versatile (and newer) lens, and so far I am pleased with it. It's a specialty filter that is useful in certain situations.

The idea behind this filter is that it has grooves in the glass that trap light and the result is a long, blue streak in the image when a light source is bright enough or is in the frame. This kind of filter is very similar to star filters that create 4-, 6- and 8-point stars, though this one creates just straight lines. When used properly this can cause some very dramatic effects in images, such as when photographing street lights or approaching cars at night.

I do need to say, though, that this kind of filter can easily be overused if not thoughtful. When used a lot, the effect can get dull and be more of an annoyance; however, when it is sparingly used it can evoke that "oh wow!" type of response for the unexpected effect.

This is a screw-on filter that will fit most standard lenses with threads. Make sure you select a filter size that is matched to your lens.

I like this lens filter and the effect it brings to the table. It is a niche product that should be used sparingly, but when used at the right time it can create an eye-popping streak effect.

I have had good success with Kingston products (in particular their SSD storage) so I was pleased to have the opportunity to work with this encrypted thumb drive. It has a lot of promise and it works better than other encrypted drives I have used. There is one drawback, at least for me - it does not support Linux (if it does, I haven't figured out how yet).

I have the 16GB version, and the thing is built like a tank. It has a metal casing around the inner workings and it can handle some abuse. That's good news if you keep these things in a briefcase or loose in a bookbag.

Setup is easy. When it is plugged into a Windows machine (I do not have access to a Mac so I cannot speak to that use case), the software is available and can be used to set up the drive with a password. That's pretty straightforward. If you forget your password, you can wipe the drive and start over but you cannot recover your data. So, choose your password wisely.

Copy rates seem to be decent - a little slower than similar-sized drives I have that aren't encrypted but not prohibitively so. It's a trade-off, and a small one at that.

When I popped this drive into my Linux machine, the kernel saw it immediately. However, all it could see was the setup partition which is approximately 100mb, a far cry from 16 GB. The drive is smart enough to hide its data from foreign OS-based systems so your data is safe. Linux is gaining users though, and being able to access the data from a Linux system would be good, even if there was a tedious process to get to the partition but still requiring a password. This is better than other encrypted drives I have used in the past which made the data scrambled but was still accessible. However, not being able to use this drive under Linux is a problem for me.

To be fair, it is not advertised as compatible with Linux.

This is a good drive and from what testing I have done it works well. That said, it does not support Linux and that is a negative for me. Hopefully Kingston will release a Linux-based version (or a software layer) for it in the future; for now it's only usable for me under Windows.

I have had excellent results with SanDisk products in the past so I anticipated a good experience with this thumb drive. So far it has met my expectations. There is some room for improvement but in operation it is a solid performer.

This is a very simple and straightforward thumb drive with no bells and whistles. It doesn't come with a cap, it doesn't extend/retract, and there isn't even an LED to indicate that it's working. However, it has been reliable up to this point and I have had no issues with transfers. The lack of an LED is mildly problematic because it is difficult to know when a transfer completes, but there are ways to work around that.

Speed is excellent. This is the fastest thumb drive I have now.

The lack of the LED, not including a cap or making the sleeve retract, and no lanyard are cut corners. All of these would make this a better product.

I am not unhappy with this drive and will use it until I wear it out. It is fast and appears to be reliable. It would have been nice if SanDisk had done more than the basics, but what is here is solid.

Lightning cables are something that we all need in the house. I selected this one with the thought of having it on the main level of the house, to be available to all of us when we want to charge our phones without hunting down a cable. So far it has worked out very well for us and is one of the better cables with which I have worked.

This is a flat cable as opposed to round and I've found this has a couple of big advantages. First, it's a lot less likely get get tangled or kinked which is great. It can be tangled, of course, but it is a lot less likely. The other big plus is that flat cables seem a lot less likely to break near the connectors for some reason. As such, I expect this cable to last for a while and to be easily accessible as long as it's not tangled up with other cables.

In use it works great. It charges my phone without issue and it also works just fine as a data cable. I did not see any mention of being it MFi certified anywhere, but it seems to be just fine regardless.

So far I have no complaints with this cable. It works, and I like the design.

This is my second TTartisan lens for my Fuji X-T3. I have been deeply impressed with my other lens, especially considering the price point, so I had high expectations for this one and it does not disappoint. It's a solid all-manual lens that performs well.

Right out of the box, I can't help but notice that this little lens has some serious heft to it. It's a very small and compact lens but it is made of metal and glass, not plastic, so the materials make it more hefty than expected. I like this; I have an expectation that if I fumble this lens it has some chance of surviving a moderate drop.

This is a fixed focal length lens with a fast F/2 aperture. It's an all manual lens that does not share data with the camera body, so if you are looking for a lens that autofocuses or sends exposure data to the camera, this is not the lens you want. If you like working with all manual lenses, or if you want to learn more about working with them, this is actually a good choice.

Exposures with this lens are dependent on the skill of the photographer, of course, but with the lens set properly exposures come out sharp, bright and with nice bokeh. There is a small bit of vignetting at the corners which is not completely unexpected, and in my case it is actually welcomes as I happen to like mild vignetting in many cases. At the widest aperture setting images are not quite as crisp and sharp as when this lens is stopped down a little, which isn't completely unexpected either. For me, F/2.8 works better, though my "default" setting is F/5.6 (true on all of my manual lenses).

The focus ring is tight and smooth and the aperture ring has a solid feel to it as well. It's an easy lens to work with and to "fine tune" when shooting.

The focal length makes this a very good choice for portraits.

I like this little lens and I will be working with it more in the coming weeks and months. For the price I have no complaints. It's not perfect, but it is better than the price suggests and it seems to be very well made.

I prefer trackballs like this one to regular mice, and I like the fact that this one is bigger than average so I decided to give it a try. So far I am pleased with it, though it isn't perfect.

DELUX is not a brand with which I was previously familiar so I wasn't sure what to expect. My requirements are fairly simple - it has to work with a dongle and it needs to work under both Linux and Windows. It definitely meets both of those requirements nicely and it has not given me any issues. I usually do not use mice with Bluetooth connections so this feature, while useful for connecting to multiple systems, is wasted on me. The dongle, however, is immediately picked up by the Linux kernel as well as by Windows and I was able to plug this in and go with no delays and no effort.

This is indeed a larger trackball and it fits my hands wonderfully. I have the hands of a gorilla and finding mice and trackballs that fit me is a challenge and I usually end up settling for something that is less than ideal for me. In this case, the trackball feels good in my hands and there is no strain on my thumbs as I don't have to stretch my hand in weird ways to reach the ball properly.

Other reviewers have mentioned that this trackball tends to skip. I have not observed this issue, though I have not had it long and I have not tried to use it with the computer more than a foot away. I also have not tried connecting via Bluetooth, which is when I have had troubles in the past with pointing devices.

One thing that would have made this trackball better would have been quiet clicking of the buttons. This is not a quiet device in use, and after using a more quiet trackball it is quite noticeable.

One important oversight is that it does not come with a battery. It takes a single AA battery, and I expected one in the box. Every other non-rechargeable pointing device I have purchased has come with a battery in the package. I am not sure why the decision was made to not include one here.

This is a nice trackball and I will be using it quite a bit, particularly on my Linux system. It's a good size for me and so far it has worked well. It would have been nice if it was quieter when clicking, and I don't know why there was no battery in the package, but these are smaller issues. I'm pleased with this trackball.

I selected this clamp for working with my mirrorless camera. There are times when clamping to a surface or a pole is more practical than setting up a tripod or monopod, so this kind of solution is useful in those cases. It's a decent clamp system and it works well, though it does require some messing with it to get used to it if you've only worked with a tripod in the past.

This idea is simple here. This is a clamp system that includes a couple of adapters for attaching cameras and accessories so that the camera can be held steady without having to set up a big, bulky tripod or having to hold the camera by hand. It comes with two clamps that can be connected via the ball joint adapter so that the system can convert to an anchor support for a pole as well (not the intended use, but practical nonetheless).

Included in the kit is a 1/4" adapter that connects to a standard camera mount (like my mirrorless), and an adapter for connecting a GoPro. It can be used directly with a cell phone, but it is not ideal for that and does require being creative with the clamps (not recommended); better is using the clamp to hold a selfie stick which in turn holds the camera.

The clamps hold tight as do the ball joints. It takes a little bit of fiddling but getting this set up exactly as desired is possible so that you can get the perfect angle. Further, the system can hold a little weight and has no trouble at all holding my mirrorless camera steady.

It seems to be made well and so far I have not had any issues with loose screws, stripped components, wobbly connectors (when properly tightened) or slipping grips. It's still early on in working with this system but so far I see no red flags.

I am happy with this clamp set-up and I will get some good use out of it. It's a practical solution when a tripod or other mount is not workable. It's not particularly expensive, either.

I work in an environment where I cannot use wireless connectivity like Wifi or Bluetooth, but I can use my smartphone. This is a problem if I want to use my iPhone 13 for music since I can’t directly connect my earphones or speakers to it. I selected this adapter for this purpose and it has answered the mail for me.

This adapter is as simple as it looks - it connects to the lightning port on an Apple device and allows for connecting a 3.5mm jack on the other. There’s no set-up required or anything - it just works. There’s a momentary initial lag as the device is recognized but that’s a very small price to pay for the functionality.

It’s designed to present the 3.5mm port at a 90 degree angle from the base of the phone. This is a lot less likely to break or get caught on something which can damage the phone. And, it’s small enough to not add much bulk to the phone.

Some real thought went into this little device. It works well and requires no real thought - just plug and play.

I have wanted a backdrop for photography for a while and chose this one based on the brand name. I have some experience with Powerextra products, in particular their replacement batteries for a digital camera I own. Based on that previous experience I thought this would be a decent frame for a backdrop. It’s mostly good and I do like it but I found an issue with the clips.

This is a fairly simple frame - two tripods with cross braces on which to hang a backdrop. It assembles fairly quickly and also tears down just as quickly. I especially like that the whole things collapses down into a small package that is roughly the same size as a fishing rod carrier and is very portable. In a pinch the whole assembly can fit wholesale inside a duffel bag with other things too, though that somewhat defeats the purpose.

This is not a heavy-duty rig which should be obvious from the price. It’s a set-up that I would say is ideal for travel as it’s relatively lightweight and easy to store, but sturdy enough to work in fairly static environments.

The main issue I have with this set-up is the set of four clips that come with it. I opened one of them and one of the tips on the clamping end popped off and went flying. It was easy enough to replace it, and it happened again on another one of the clips. I realized two things about the clips - three of the four clips were assembled incorrectly which makes this much more likely to happen, and the tips can be lost fairly easily. The clips are the most easily replaceable part of the whole assembly so in the grand scheme of things this is not a showstopper but more thought could have been put into the clamp design (and assembly) without increasing costs appreciably.

This is not a perfect rid for setting up backdrops but it works well enough and the cost is very reasonable. Pay attention to the clip assembly, though, and ensure that the tips are installed correctly.

I have gotten more into creative photography and I have enjoyed playing with lens filters like these. I have worked with star filters in the past and I thought it might be fun to experiment with this light streak filter as well. So far I have no complaints, though it is the type of filter that should be used sparingly.

This is a gold streak filter that works in the same way as star filters, only it channels light in a straight line across the frame instead of in multiple directions. That is, it can make lights look smeared as if swept from one direction in a straight line. The color of the filter lines alters the light slightly and it has a mildly warming effect.

Some thought went into this filter and it allows for turning the filter (similar to a CPL) so that it can channel light in any single direction.

As with any filter like this, it should be used sparingly. It is possible to have too much of a good thing and as such this can easily be overdone. When used properly and used infrequently it can make some very striking and impactful photos.

It seems to be well made. There are no hitches in the turn when making directional adjustments, and the glass does not rattle loosely in the metal frame. I have found no damage to the glass or metal right out of the package either.

One question that might come up is, why should you use this kind of filter then it is easy to do the same thing in software? The answer is straightforward - it's fun!

This is very much a fun and useful filter but it is a special-use thing that should be used with some restraint. It seems to be well made and it does generate the desired effects. It is not particularly expensive either which is a plus.

I needed a second battery for my Fuji X-T3 and I really wasn't excited by the price of the NP-W126S battery, so I looked for third-party replacements. After scraping user forums online and doing some additional research I settled on this one from Nitecore. It has proven to be every bit as good as Fuji brand batteries, and in some ways it's a little better.

I knew Nitecore as a manufacturer of flashlights and other light sources in particular. I was previously unaware of their batteries, so I was pleasantly surprised to discover that they had a battery that was an exact fit for my camera. It does fit perfectly, too - pops in and out without fuss and fits the charger without issue.

One of the issues with third-party batteries is that the camera will sometimes complain about it and throw up a message about a non-standard battery. I was initially concerned that this one would give me that issue but it has not - my camera accepts it without complaint and it just works.

I have been working with it for several months now, and it seems to actually last longer than the original battery that came with my camera (an actual NP-W126S battery). I have fully charged it one time, and since then I have taken well over 200 pictures with my camera (probably closer to 450) and it still has roughly 80% of the charge which is a big improvement. The thing that seems to drain my Fuji battery fastest is powering the camera on and off; this Nitecore battery seems to handle those cycles better.

It has overcharge protection and it stops charging when it reaches full capacity, even on the Fuji charger. I was concerned about using it on the original charger and considered getting the Nitecore charger to go with this battery, but it's perfectly happy on the Fuji charger.

I like the harder shell on this battery as compared to the original Fuji battery, Eventually this battery will fail; when it does, I am optimistic that the hard shell will keep it from swelling quickly so I can get it out of the camera when it finally starts to fail.
