It is extremely lightweight, I don't feel it added any bulk or weight. it is a little bigger than described so theres about an inch above and a half inch around of extra material. That doesn't bother me but it is good to know it isnt snug on a 15.6" laptop. overall I think this is an amazing case for the money and I'm happy with this purchase! I would 100% reccomend it!

This keyboard cover is good for the price. The pink is beautiful in person and from far away but unfortunately not as nice up close. It looks like my cover was either painted/printed a tad bit off because many of the keys have a white line on the right side where it should still be pink. There's also some extra silicone kind of hanging off the edge of the 0, ., and enter keys on the number panel. Other than the minor issues it seems ok! I just recieved it a few minutes ago and put it on so I can't really speak for the adhesion or durability so I will update my review as time passes. I'd say for the price it's worth it!
Works well and looks nice - just what I was after.

I wanted a bigger second monitor at home since I do some graphic design work and find it much easier on the larger screen. I am not one of those people that cares much about buying the most advanced specs on monitors. Does it work well without glitches? Yes? Perfect. Does the display look good with no obvious color issues? Yes? Perfect. Am I able to sit at it for long periods and do my work successfully? Yes! And, it was a good deal, too, so I'm happy.

I have had a Kindle Fire for years (I'm on my second one), but before I went on vacation to Hawaii (where I expected to be reading in direct sunlight - something the Fire is not good for), I ordered this Paperwhite. You absolutely can read in direct sunlight with this. The battery life is PHENOMENAL! And, my eyes do not get tired like they usually do when I read on the Fire or my laptop. Despite not *really* wanting to spend the money when I already had a perfectly functioning Fire, this has become my go-to device. I love it!
I use this as a second screen with my Macbook Pro 15 and it works perfectly (and makes working from home a lot easier). I recommend it!

I was actually in the market for a to-quality leather laptop case, but everything I found either wouldn't fit my Macbook Pro 15", or was far too large and heavy. When I found this one at such as reasonable cost, I was dubious that I would like it. Surprise: I love it! It's well-made and the perfect size for my Macbook. My boss (who only buys luxury Italian brands) noticed it and liked it as well. For the money, you can't beat it.
While it was slightly smaller than I expected, it was a fantastic deal for the money. It's every bit as nice as the $100 bags from a well-known camera bag maker.

Purchased to replace damaged pads on an older set of SteelSeries headphones that are no longer made. These fit perfectly. Slightly tricky to install but they do stretch slightly. Once on, they are secure and comfortable. They appear to be well made and are reasonably priced. Shipped quickly. Time will tell. Extremely pleased so far.

I selected this tripod to try out on my recent Alaska cruise, but ended up not using it during the trip due to the weight. It would have easily tipped my luggage weight over the 50 lbs limit. Otherwise it is really nice though for an amateur photographer like me. It's sturdy, holds my camera well, and I'm able to take some neat wildlife photos at home. It has a nice carry case. It works great for home photos & I'll probably take it on trips where we don't travel by air, but I'll look into budgeting a carbon fiber tripod for other trips.

I selected this headset for my daughter, and she really likes it. The sound quality is great, and it's very comfortable. The changing colors are also fun too. The only thing my daughter wishes is that she had the ability to go wireless, as she has to remove them every time she needs to get up from her desk. But otherwise, it's a great headset.

I like to play computer games, and when I'm playing I usually go on for quite a long session. So an ergonomic mouse is a must have for me. I selected this mouse to go with my laptop and it's working really well. It's comfortable, reactive (no delay or drag) and the battery life is quite good. It fits nicely in my laptop bag. I also tend to be kind of hard on my mouse, so I usually have to replace them every 2 years or so. With the price so reasonable, I don't mind having to replace this mouse.

When I received my new laptop, I was initially dismayed to see how few USB ports it had. Not only do I like to use a mouse rather than the track pad, I also like to use a cooling tray when I'm playing games on the laptop. This USB hub is perfect for me. I'm able to plug in the bluetooth dongle for my mouse, and the cooling tray cord. It's nice and compact, fits easily in my laptop bag.

I selected this rolling backpack to carry my laptop and paperwork while I travel. It has worked out really great, especially on my most recent trip. It fits quite a few items, I had my laptop and my accordion file folder inside along with some personal items and it was easy to move around. It has loads of pockets to place most of the items I need handy while I'm traveling. I'm also able to maneuver it quite well along with my suitcase. It fit in the overhead compartment of the airplane with ease, and rolls with no issues.

This lovely smartwatch packs all the bells and whistles of a name brand, but not at name brand price. The watch and the app were easy to set up and use, I really like the feature where I can use a photo on my phone as the watchface. It does a great job with sleep tracking, steps, and exercise. I can also set it to notify me and show texts from my phone. The alarm feature is nice, it wakes me up without waking my spouse too.

Even though the O2 and blood pressure aren't really for medical purposes, just for informational, they do seem to be close to what my actual readings are. So they do seem fairly accurate. I also like how there are a variety of exercises to choose from. The app links to Google Fit too, which is really nice. Battery life is quite good, I'm able to go a week before I need to charge again, and the watch charges to full within an hour or so.

I've tried a few different non-name brand smartwatches and this one by far is my favorite. I would definitely recommend it to others.

There are a lot of things I like about this cooling pad. It has fun led lights I can set to a variety of color patterns, keeps my laptop cool, and I can raise up the back so my hand position is more ergonomic. I also like how small it is, I can fold it flat and easily take with me when I travel. It's made well, I've had no issues with it so far. The fan is a little noisy, but it doesn't bother me that much.

I would not recommend this bag for laptops bigger than 14 inches. It's nicely constructed, but on the small side. It is what it says though, durable and water resistant. It fits my 14 inch Asus nicely, plus the power supply & the mouse. It also has some pockets that could fit other items like your phone, pens, etc.

I've tried a variety of budget smart watches, and this one by Dr.Viva has become my favorite. It's very comfortable, great flexible band, no issues with feeling like it's pressing into my wrist bones. The screen display is a good size without being too large, perfect for smaller wrists.

The Zeroner app has been fantastic, no problems. It accurately tracks my steps, sleep & oxygen. I like how it has a variety of exercises for me to document. The battery life is a big winner. I recharge the smart watch once a week, compared to twice a week with the other watches I've tried before. I was disappointed that I don't have the option to have my own picture as the screen display, but the app still has plenty of screens to choose from.

If you're like me and don't want to spend an exorbitant price on a smart watch, but would still like to enjoy the features of a smart watch this one would be a great option.

I selected this radio to keep with the rest of our emergency supply kit. If you'd like to do the same, I'd recommend you charge the radio first before putting it away. You'll be working the hand crank for hours if you don't, and that's no fun if the power is out. Sound works pretty well, the light works great too. You'll want to hang onto the instruction because the buttons for the radio are not intuitive. I like how it has a usb output if you need to recharge your phone, but I too wish there was a storage area for the charging cable. I don't get a lot of direct sun where I am, so I don't think the solar panel would be that helpful for me, especially if there's a storm that knocks out the power. For the price though, I think this radio would be a good addition to your emergency kit.

This smart watch has quite a few of the features that the name brand watches do, but without the name brand price. It keeps track of your steps, although it's a little over-sensitive and will count steps if all you do is move your arms like folding clothes or such. The sleep tracker is accurate, and so is the oxygen meter. I like how it has a variety of exercise types to choose from. The customizable watch face feature is great to. I like being able to use my favorite vacation picture as my watch face. I'd recommend this watch to anyone who'd like to try out a smart watch without paying a high price.

This smart watch packs in a lot of great features for a really inexpensive price. The Inxfit app is very user friendly, easy to set up and quickly pairs to the watch. I like how I'm able to set goals, keep track of my sleep and activity. Steps & sleep readings are accurate, no odd variations. I like how it has a variety of watch faces, and the ability to make my own from a favorite photo from my phone. The watch is comfortable to wear, even for sleeping. No need to buy the expensive brand name smart watches, this one has them beat!

I selected this bluetooth adapter for my daughter's computer so that she could use her wireless headphones with it. Overall, it does mostly do what it claims, but there are some issues. It found her headphones right away, but uses 5.0 tech, not 5.1. The sound works great if she remains in her room, but will encounter static at distances much less than 65'. The price is too high for what the adapter can do, and the static is very annoying.

If you cringe at the $$$ price of the brand name smart watches, I think this one by Eurans is a pretty good value. It still have quite a few features that are really nice. It tracks fitness, sleep, heart rate & O2 monitoring like a champ. The step counter is good too, fairly accurate compared to the Fitbit I previously wore. Pairing the watch to the app was a breeze.

I like how there's a good variety of fitness options to choose from, both indoor and outdoor. That's great when like me you like to do different types of exercise through the week to keep from getting bored or losing motivation. I'm very happy with the Fitdock app. No weird translation issues like with other apps I've tried. It's easy to understand, and it works well. It's fun to be able to use a picture from my phone as the background screen on my watch. The silent alarm works well too, it wakes me without waking my spouse, a great feature when couples are on different work schedules.

A couple of features I wish the smart watch had- the ability to monitor blood pressure (though I know it's not really a medically approved method), and a reminder to drink water. But these don't really detract from how nice this watch is, so I didn't remove any stars for it. I think this smart watch would make a great gift for someone who is interested in smart watches, but concerned about paying the high price for the brand name models.

There are a lot of things I like about this smartwatch. The face is smaller than other smartwatches I've looked at and tried, about 1.09" which is perfect for me. Bigger faces like many smartwatches out there are uncomfortable for me to wear, especially when I'm trying to sleep. The design of the watch is really pretty, and I like how the neutral color goes with many outfits. One thing I do wish is that the watchband was changeable so that I could change it if the band wore out or broke (or if I wanted a different style). Most of the smartwatches with changeable bands are those with the large face, a little disappointing. Battery power is good. I use the smartwatch quite often so I tend to hook it up to the battery charger twice a week. I like how I could choose from a variety of screen displays to fit what my preferences are.

The app this smartwatch uses is great, the Da Fit app. It's super easy to use, you don't have to use Bluetooth to find the watch, you just use the app to find it. I like how it has a variety of physical activity you can choose to monitor, jogging, biking, walking, etc. The sleep feature is pretty good, the biggest detractor is that it only follows typical sleeping hours. It won't work for anyone who sleeps different hours due to working night shift. Hopefully they'll update that in the app someday. The blood pressure feature seems to be pretty accurate to what the doctor tells me my blood pressure is.

Since I really don't want to put out the money for the brand name smartwatches, I am very pleased that I can still enjoy quite a few of the features for a more reasonable price. I'd recommend this watch and it would make a great gift.

Update- After a couple weeks of use, the on/off button on the side of the watch popped off and a spring came out. It's so tiny I'm unable to find it. I wasn't using it excessively, so I'm disappointed that something on the watch would break within weeks of use. It's a really nice watch, and they have great customer care so hopefully my issue is not a common problem.

If sticker shock with the brand name smartwatches have kept you from buying one for yourself, this watch packs a lot of punch for a very decent price. It has many of the options that the brand name watches have, but easier on the budget. Sleep monitoring, activity tracking, silent alarms, the weather and many more. It's a great watch. Battery life is on par with other watches, lasting close to a week.

Two small detractors that keep me from making this watch my favorite. The watch face is huge, too big for my wrist. On the one hand, it's nice because I can easily see it. But after wearing it for a while it's a little uncomfortable due to the size and I'm contemplating getting a smartwatch with a smaller face. The second problem is the alarm setting. I have an alarm set for 6am Monday-Friday. But the alarm is going off 6am Tuesday-Saturday. I've confirmed that the date is correct on my watch & phone so I'm not sure what's going on. Maybe it's an issue with the DaFit app? That aside, I still really like the watch.

I've been using this cable on my nightstand to keep my phone charged for a couple of years now, and I'm very happy with it. I don't have issues with the cable kinking near the connectors, and I prefer braided cables to plastic. I plug in my phone before bed, and it's fully charged by the time I get up in the morning.

Sadly this mouse did not give me the quality that I was expecting from a Corsair product. Their keyboards are great, but this mouse just doesn't stand up to the use that I need. It's a gorgeous mouse, and a comfortable ergonomic style. But the battery life was abysmal & the responsiveness was iffy. I ended up getting frustrated and going back to my Logitech mouse.

I have a nice new gaming laptop and one of the first things I wanted for it was a good cooling tray. This cooling pad by Aicheson does the trick and it's reasonably priced. It does a great job of keeping the temp down, the lights are fun & I like how it has tilt options. It fits nicely in my laptop bag too.

I selected these headphones for my daughter, as her old Sony headphones were falling apart. She likes these a lot, they're similar in style to her old favorites, plus they have pink accents which she loves. The sound is good, they're comfortable, and they're priced reasonably.

I am very happy with this braided USB to micro-USB. I took it to work and connected it to my computer so I can keep my phone charged up. It's great. The braided cable is awesome, I want to upgrade all of my charging cables to the type with a braided cable. Especially for the great price of the AmazonBasics brand. I would definitely recommend this cable to others.

Installation was a breeze, I followed the suggestion of installing them in a humid bathroom. That little tip really does help to cut down or even eliminate the lint. The anti-glare & anti-fingerprint finish is great, looks really nice.

This laptop bag by Solo is nicely designed and well made. I like all the pockets & compartments it has, plenty of room for my laptop, tablet & accessories. The additional pockets for holding documents or ID is a nice feature, I also like the back strap for securing the bag to my luggage handle. As for the RFID blocking pocket, I'm not sure how helpful it is or not, but it doesn't detract from the bag so I don't mind it. The messenger bag is a pretty decent bag for the price.

I have been through many different types of in-ear headphones over the decades, and these by Audio-Technica are by far the best I have ever used. Not only is the sound amazing, they are so incredibly comfortable too. I really like the wrap around cables, they are a great feature. The headphones are so comfortable too. One of my biggest complaints with ear-bud style headphones is that they start to hurt when wearing them. I haven't had that issue with these headphones. With the sound & the comfort, I think they're definitely worth the price.

There is so much to love about this USB cable. Not only does it have the braided cable, but each end connection has extra enforcement that helps to avoid breaking after period of use. It's well worth the price, after dealing with cheap USB cables that come with my devices that crack where the cable meets the connector. It's expensive, but so is replacing those cheap plastic USB cables multiple times over the life of a device.

One thing I wish OtterBox would do, is to offer these in various lengths. I'd like to use one to connect my phone to my computer, so a shorter cable would be nice for that.

My web cam bit the dust when it slipped and fell off my monitor, so I needed to pick up a new one. I decided to stick with Logitech, because I've been happy with their products for the most part. Installation was simple, I plugged it in and it was ready in a few seconds. The only thing I don't care for is the clip design. It's the same style as my previous camera (the C310), and the loose design doesn't make for a secure fit on top of the monitor. That's the reason why I went for the cheaper version this time, but hopefully I won't have another problem with clumsiness. Otherwise, I think it's a great camera.

I'm using the micro SD card with the adapter in my Canon PowerShot Elph 360. I love how much storage I have for photos, and the quality of the photos are great. It's easy to use, reasonably priced, and it's a brand I trust. I've been a fan of SanDisk products for years, and would recommend this SD card.

They are simple and inexpensive earbuds that work as designed. Sound is crisp and clear. I especially like the small clip to secure the headphone wire to my shirt collar. That clip is my favorite feature of these headphones, I wish my others had this clip as well, but I can switch it to my other headphones, a nice touch. This is a good set to have for backup, or for when you don't want to spend much.

Set up was an absolute breeze. I unhooked my old Samsung 22" flat LED monitor, plugged in this beauty and it started right up. Settings were off at first, but after fiddling with them, I am very pleased with how great it looks. Colors look amazing, very sharp and crisp. I thought the curve in the screen might bug my eyes, but they adjusted to it within a couple of hours. It doesn't bother me at all now.

I've been messing around with all of usual things I do on the computer, and I am liking all of them on this new monitor. I played some of my favorite games, wow. I am seriously blown away. Watched a couple episodes of Game of Thrones, and it looks incredible on the screen. Web browsing is very nice as well. I've been checking out the "Eye Saver" mode too. It's a little different, the slight yellow tinge I see while using it might take some getting used to. But, if it will help with eye strain I will definitely continue to work with it.

I've been a Samsung fan for monitors for a while now, and the CF591 is no exception. This is a fantastic monitor.

I have two of the Seagate 1TB external hard drives (one for me, one for my husband). We've been extremely happy with them so I was eager to try out the 5TB. I stored copies of all the photos I have from over the last two decades, family videos, scanned copies of important documents & files. It's amazing how much the drive can store. It doesn't bother me that it has to be powered by an ac adapter because I have it connected to my desktop computer. File transfer is fast, and luckily I've had no issues with heat. However, I still make sure nothing falls on or covers any part of the drive, just in case. I think it's a great drive for the price.

I love this trackball so much I've bought one for my husband. I also bought a new one for myself, after my previous Kensington trackball started to fail after 3-4 years of use. One of my favorite features of it is how it can be easily switched for those of us who are left handed. I also like the scroll ring. The ball is easily removed for cleaning, and the shape is very comfortable. I've tried other trackballs that make my wrists ache. If I get 3-4 years of use out of this one I think $30 is well worth the price.

We have two Kindle Fire users in the family, our teen daughters, so I was looking forward to trying out this case. I was so pleased that I hopped on Amazon and bought a 2nd in blue. It's sturdy, and fits the Kindle Fire HD perfectly. The cutouts on the back match exactly where the volume & on/off buttons are, and also for the speakers. My daughters like how they can easily have their Kindle in whatever direction they want, vertical to read a book, or propped horizontal to watch a video.

The price of the case is right in line with other similar cases. It's strong & sturdy, not flimsy. I would definitely recommend this case for your Kindle Fire HD.

After a dismal experience with a Patriot brand micro SD card (card died after a few weeks) I was eager to try the Samsung brand. I am very pleased with the card. I use it to save books, PDF files, & photos on my tablet. I have a Samsung Galaxy 2.0, a nice tablet but with limited storage space. By using this micro SD card I'm able to utilize my tablet more and get what I feel is full use out of it. The price was reasonable for the amount of storage on it, installation was quite simple, and it works extremely well on my tablet. I plan on buying a couple more for our cell phones.

we are using the extender in a 2000 sqft one story home. We have our router set up in our family room at one end of the house, because that is where the cable connection is. Prior to obtaining the extender, we had issues getting a good signal at the other end of the house. Our laptops & tablets would consistently lose the signal or lag.

The Netgear Wi-Fi Extender has ended those issues, and we now have consistent signal everywhere in the house. Setup was simple, we followed the steps on the handy "Getting Started" installation paperwork. The extender has been placed at the midpoint of the house in the living room, so that there will be good coverage everywhere. I am able to get a good, consistent signal even at the very edge of the house in the master bathroom. No more issues for the laptops or tablets, we are quite pleased.

Luckily I had nothing important on the card, just some saved tv shows for my tablet. It worked fine for a few months, then just suddenly stopped working. Although I've been mucking around on a computer for many years now, this was my first venture into the tablet venue. I wasn't really sure what to buy. Do I go all out, buy a larger one with all the bells & whistles for the price of a base model laptop? Or do I stick with something simple & inexpensive?

I decided to go with the Samsung Galaxy Tab 2. The price was a definite consideration, I liked that it was under $200. I preferred to stick with name brand, as I've had too many friends who went with an inexpensive brand that broke within a few months. The size seemed sufficient for me to play some of the fun apps & keep notes for school.

It's been around 6 months since I first bought the tablet, and I'm overall pleased with it. I do wish it had two things. More storage, because the OS takes up a great deal of space. In hindsight, I would have paid more to have 16GB rather than 8. Also, I wish the charging port was a micro USB instead of 30 pin data port. My husband's Samsung Note has the micro USB and so does my daughter's Nexus 7. It would be really nice to be able to use other charging cords like they do (my husband can use his phone charger) than having to make sure I don't EVER misplace this one.

But for a simple tablet from a trusted brand, I do think the Samsung Galaxy Tab 2 is a good choice.

I tend to use a simpler camera for now, I'm not into multiple lenses (yet!) so right now I have room for both my camera & it's simple gear, plus my wallet as well. So I'm able to condense my bags when we go to Disney, which is really nice. When I do decide to start trying out the various lenses, there is plenty of room for them.

So if you're looking for a good camera bag that won't break your budget, stick with Case Logic. I've been very pleased with all their products so far.

Because of the daily use during the week, they need to charge them every couple of days. But that is a simple matter to take care of. Once they've finished their homework they plug them in, then in the morning unplug before we head off for school. I have noticed that due to the frequent use, the numbers & letters have worn off of most of the keys. That could be a bit of an issue but the girls have memorized which key is for which letter or number.

I like how there's little to no glare in the sun, the Kindle is easier to read than other readers or a tablet. After doing some research, I read that these headphones are the best "bang for your buck" earbuds and so far, they aren't wrong. This product does some with six different silicon eartips, an small instruction booklet, and a small but durable pouch to put your eartips and buds in. It took me about five minutes find the perfect removable eartips for my ears. It would have been shorter but I was afraid of tearing the silicon tips (so far none have ripped). Everybody's ears are different but my ears prefer the smallest snowman shape ones for both my right and left ear (Pictures of the tips can be found in the 'Wired' only version of this product).

They are easy to clean and the remote is secure (meaning that the remote button or volume slider won't move or activate if it accidentally hits your clothes or something). I haven't used the microphone yet. These things are very secure once you install them in your ears. You can talk, yawn, chew gum, run, jump and drink water and these tips wouldn't budge (you can take them out easily though). The sound quality and noise blocking are great too for when I run. It also works well for people that wear glasses like me.

However I have two small issues with this product. One is that the wire is a little long for me but it usually doesn't get in your way (only once so far but this was my second time using them). You may experience burning in your ears. I did at first when I was trying to find the best way to wear them. For me (using the smallest snowman ones), You just put them before the ear canal so the silicon tips rest comfortably in your ears. Don't push/force them in your ears because that will cause your ears to burn.

In conclusion, if you're looking for the best sleek 'bang for your buck' earbuds that stay secure during rigorous activity who doesn't mind a little burning in your ear canals at first, then I would recommend this product and I'll probably buy it again when/if this product wears out.

Edit: Just after a month of use the the remote button is a little glitchy. Before it could be resting against by chest while running and it would work fine. Now while running, I have to pull it about 5 inches away from my body and point the the top of the headset (where it branches off into two) at about a 45 degree angle in order to pause/skip a song. It's kind of cumbersome and if it didn't do this then I'd definitely rate it higher.

Edit: The sellers were very prompt and understanding with my situation and I got a new pair for free (under warranty). I've been using them for a couple of months and I haven't noticed any problems with them.

I’ve had this SSD for a few days and I also have a 1TB 970 Evo Plus and 1TB 860 Evo and all of them are great! But they do have their drawbacks too.

This drive does really well with SMALL (under 15Gb) workloads. The speeds are right up there (~500MB/s R/W) with my 860 Evo until it gets to about ~14GB at which point it slows down drastically. This is fine for things like boot, games, apps, and most programs.

However, if you do heavy workloads like video editing, file transfers, etc,. where you are regularly moving large (15GB+) files around this is NOT the drive for you. If you are a “heavy” user I highly recommend the 860 Pro. It can keep up those high R/W speeds without slowing down after ~15GB. It will maintain full speed throughout the duration of whatever you are doing.

With that said this is a great drive for light/moderate workloads (gaming, web browsing, small work files, etc.,) and it is at a price that gives you excellent value and quality for your money.

I also really love the Samsung Magician software. It’s basically the main reason why 3/5 of my drives are Samsung. Samsung is also known for making reliable, high quality products. Yes there is a premium compared to cheaper drives but you’re paying that little bit extra for quality & reliability.

I took off 1 Star on this review though because Samsung doesn’t include any of the cables or mounting screws which just doesn’t make sense to me. C’mon Samsung start adding that stuff! I would’ve happily paid a couple dollars more for it and it wouldn’t have cost Samsung that much so they could’ve made a little bit of extra profit by adding it.

I still recommend this drive though and would buy it or the 860 Evo again if I needed more storage.

Not much to say about this product. It works great with my Samsung 860 Evo and that's all I wanted it to do. If you need a good SATA cable I would recommend this one. It's a fair price for what you get.

Update: I see a lot of people complaining about the drive capacity being “wrong” (465gb instead of 500gb or 960gb instead of 1TB) and to those people I highly recommend going to YouTube and searching “What is Overprovisioning?” and clicking on the link by TechQuickie.

Samsung is NOT falsely advertising. The drive DOES in fact come with the advertised space it’s just that in order for it to work properly and perform optimally it requires approximately 10% of the capacity to be overprovisioned free space.

This is a really great SATA SSD for the price. It's perfect for storing games that have long load times without paying a fortune for an NVMe SSD of equal capacity. I highly recommend it for people like me who need more space for games, projects, and other things like that who want them to load quickly. You can get an HDD like a WD Black for cheaper but the loading times will be much longer and for those who dont like to wait for long load screens this is a perfect choice.

Also don't forget to enable RAPID mode. It uses RAM to speed up the programs & applications that you have been using recently. My CrystalDisk benchmark shows how fast it is with RAPID mode enabled.

These earbuds combine incredible sound in a stylish and functional package. I would give these more than 5 stars if I could. I had high expectations before trying these, especially in view of the price, and these earbuds blew those away.

Bang & Olufsen's engineers magically crammed a high-end sound system into a lightweight, wireless earbud. You have to hear them to believe how amazing these sound - clean, clear music across an impressively wide range. I noticed details for the first time in songs that I have heard many times before.

Beyond the sound, the craftsmanship and overall product design are outstanding. I don't know about the electronics as only time will tell, but the earbuds and the case themselves look like they will hold up to regular use without any issues. The leather and brushed aluminum on the case adds an extra-premium feel to the product.

Also, at first I thought the charging capability of the case was a bit gimmicky, but I quickly realized my error. It is so convenient to know that the earbuds are fully charged whenever I want to use them. I don't have a Qi charger, so I haven't taken advantage of the full wireless capability. But for me, it is not a big deal to use the USB cord when I need to occasionally charge the case.

To give some context, this is not a product I would have considered purchasing on my own. I've always thought of earbuds as cheap, portable ways to listen to music while working out or on the go - situations where the background noise means that you can't appreciate high-quality sound. However, after jumping at the chance to try these, they have completely changed my perspective on what earbuds can do. Excellent sound quality is available in a highly portable, convenient product.

The only downside I have experienced is that the touch controls take some time to get used to. I had trouble figuring it out at first, but after a few days I can usually get them to do what I intend to do on the first try. I prefer the minimalistic design, so this learning curve is not a significant issue for me.

I also like the Bang & Olufsen music app that allows selection of different listening modes that vary between - "warm", "excited", "relaxed", or "bright" sound profiles. Switching between the modes really gives the sound a different character. My favorite feature on the app, however, is the ability to select "transparency" of the music. A higher level of transparency amplifies your surroundings so you can hear what is going on around you. This does not give you spy-gadget levels of hearing, but it noticeably amplifies background sounds. I've been using these headphones at work, and I can easily hear when my phone rings or when someone knocks on my office door.

Last, the excellent sound quality carries over to phone calls. I have no trouble hearing the other person on the line, which is not always the case with the built-in speaker on my iPhone. Also the people I have talked to have had heard me clearly. This was an unexpected bonus, and I actually prefer to use the earbuds for calls now.

TL;DR: If you can afford these, you won't regret it.

Was actually pleased by the caps when they arrived. I used to be particular about keycap quality, but in the last few years the quality and cost of keycaps have been awesome; I'm so thrilled about those new to the hobby (although it's still expensive). When GMK 9009 was originally announced, I thought it was the perfect modern edition of classic beige. Everyone should have a good classic beige set, and 9009 is it.

Right now, my workhorse keyboard is a polycarbonate 910 with Cherry MX Grays and third-party springs (I forget the weight). Typing on it is a dream every day, and the keycaps can enhance the experience. I prefer PBT on this keyboard because it has a more pleasant, thocky sound than ABS caps. There's also a bit of tactile pushback with ABS, at least from what I noticed. While I love 9009, I'm not thrilled about ABS. Sure, ABS is cool and develops a nice shine based on use, but I prefer the consistent feel of PBT; having some keycaps stripped of their coating from use while others still feel new can throw me off. All that to say that I'm glad I was able to get this 9009 set in PBT. I was very hesitant, though, because the price for this many dye-sublimated, PBT keycaps was too good to be true.

When the package arrived, I was disappointed to find that there was no shipping box. The keycaps arrived in their manufacturer box with a shipping label slapped on it. Not only can that increase the chances of theft, but the shipping label covers the rendering that shows all the keycaps included. So now I'll have to resort to the listing to see what all should be in the box. However, nothing appears damaged. The keycaps come in wonderfully secure, plastic trays, three stacked on each other. There are a lot of keycaps here, so most keyboards should be covered. Of course, not everything will be perfect; for my 910, the Home cap is taller than the rest of the row, and there is no 1u Tab cap, nor a R1-height Fn cap. There's only one 1u blank keycap, which doesn't sit flush with the rest of the caps in its row. Minor gripes because I know my layout is particular.

But, again, there still is a great amount of keycaps so I'm sure most boards will be covered.

Now, as for the keycaps themselves. As I mentioned, I was very hesitant when the package arrived, but overall I'm pleasantly surprised. The keycaps are slightly thinner than enjoyPBT and BSP caps, and the stem can be a bit snug, but not too tight so that they don't come off easily. The sublimation is very good; I haven't noticed any that appear sloppy. Some num pad legends seem a bit thinner than others, but overall the legends are consistent and have that Cherry-legend appearance.

I wish there were more color options here, but for the price I can't complain. Truly, at $40, this set is an amazing bang for the buck.

Before ordering this telescope, I researched the difference between reflector and refractor telescopes. The last telescope I had was a hand-me-down (I forget which brand) refractor telescopes. I've developed a strong passion for everything beyond earth, so I looked forward to using this telescope--my first reflector telescope.

Because the telescope requires assembly, I pulled out the instructions...and became very confused. While some of the parts looked similar to what was in the box, I quickly realized the instructions were for a completely different model. Even if these were the right instructions, the photographs provided were taken by a camera and not the clearest quality; good assembly instructions usually have computer-generated images or diagrams, not photographs taken by a camera. The rest of the instruction manual was a general guide on using telescopes, though a much better quick-start guide can be found easily online.

So, with some trial and error, and a lot more time than I anticipated building the telescope, I finally got it assembled. And just in time too, because the moon had just crossed the window of the room I build the telescope in, and the moon was in great view. The opportunity also let me play around with the features of the telescope. It's not very easy to use because the stand is *very* wobbly. The counterweights are too much for the tripod, and the tripod should have used a better, more sturdy material. Despite all that, it's super fun to use. It comes with decent eyepieces to play around with; I didn't know how much of a difference eyepieces can make. With this telescope, I was able to view details of the moon for the first time. It really is just a big ball of rock spinning around.

Having recently dug my music collection (odd how we go back into hobbies after years of stagnation), I took time to curate my setup (and by setup I mean my Note8 with a USB DAC) for optimal listening. Until recently, but "best" headphones were my Shure Aonic 4, which are excellent for the price range. The cable it comes with is okay, but preferably replaceable. It comes with an inline mic and makes a lot of feedback-noise when moved. I know cables are a mixed bag when it comes to audio equipment, so I shied away for years. But rather than place the emphasis on audio-quality improvement when looking at cables, I realized I'd rather get a cable if it looks and feels good. This one fit the ticket.

This is the only cable I have that's meant to be swapped with MMCX in-ear headphones. They pair well with the Aonic 4. First, I'll get the problems I have out of the way.

Since this cable is meant to connect with around-the-ear IEMs, there's a plastic wrap near each MMCX adapter. It makes wearing around the ears easier, but putting them on initially takes a few tries. They are easy to tangle, even if I use the "roadie wrap." Putting them on while on the go proved to be suboptimal; I have to be sitting or standing to put them on.

Sometimes I get some feedback noise, but rarely. Definitely not the same as the stock cable that comes with the Aonic 4.

The biggest problem I have is that the end connection disconnects nearly every time I use the cable. Having a modular cable is awesome, but the connection from the cable to the audio jack doesn't lock. I expected there to be a click, indicating it's on and snug, but no such thing. Since I use this cable while on the go, it's connected to my phone, which rests in my pocket. At least once the cable end will come loose. It's easy to press back in (just a little nudge will do), but it is rather annoying.

Now for the good.

The cable feels awesome. I get now why people prefer to upgrade certain cables. I care very little for how much the audio quality is "improved" (there's too much immeasurable subjectivity in that area), but having a cable that doesn't tangle easily and is very light makes enough of a difference to justify the upgrade. The cable is soft to the touch, though I don't doubt its ruggedness in the long term. The MMCX connectors snap satisfactorily into the Shure IEMs; at least those haven't come loose. The metal ends and Y-splitter are very nice and definitely attribute the cable with a premium look.

This cable has sold me on the reasons to upgrade headphone cables.

Usually low is enough. However, I can't stand using this for a while because it's sufferingly loud. My cat runs away whenever I turn this on. Honestly, it's almost as loud as my vacuum cleaner. I took it to my office and use it only for about 5 seconds. Also, because it's unbalanced, it becomes very heavy at the top and awkward to move when dusting.
It's an awesome ornament that definitely attracts attention. To work, it should be fully charged and hung on the tree; it works exactly as the description states.
Though we don't use this for data, the charging ability is great. We finally can fast-charge our devices, and the build quality feels like it should last a while.

This neck fan works well, but it's a bit weak. I still get sweaty in the areas it blows cool air. The neck fan fits our youngest daughter as well as me. The rotation of the fans isn't the best, but at least they reach where we'd like.

The binoculars work well for everyday use. I've used it to see blocks away from my home, as well as for some stargazing. The binoculars aren't too heavy, but the angle can be a bit uncomfortable on my nose.

The cable itself works marvelously, and fits snug and secure in my TV. The only issue is that, because of the cable material, it's somewhat difficult to get into tight corners. I route cables from my mounted TV to an entertainment center on the floor, which has several holes for cable management. Getting the cable through the entertainment center was a bit of a hassle.
Great cable and durably made. Has been used in various plugs, homes, and vehicles, and charges without issue.

Wonderful replacement tips for my Shure Aonic 4. The sound is comfortable, and the feeling is soothing. They're not a perfect fit for the Shure, even though they're supposed to be compatible; the tips come off freely if pulled, but surprisingly they stay on when removing the earbuds from the within the ears.

These aren't just for consoles; we paired this with a computer, and it worked flawlessly. The comfort-level is very good; I didn't get fatigue after wearing it. The mic works well, and can be tucked in when not in use.
They're bulky, so a bit distracting if you're using them to chat.

This is the first mesh system I've used. I had a Linksys router and an Asus router before this, both installed with third-party firmware. After the Asus upgrade, I used the Linksys router as a repeater. The signal was okay; considering I had Xfinity 250Mbps, the Asus worked fantastically, while the Linksys trailed behind. We live in an old apartment building with thick, plaster walls, so signal can be very spotty.

With this mesh system, I saw a huge upgrade the first week. Setup was very easy; quick instructions are provided. As soon as the setup was complete, I delved into the firmware. I recall being a little disappointed as I was used to the Asus custom firmware (Asuswrt-Merlin). The Asus firmware "just werqed." I run a small server, and setup was super easy with the Asus. With the Netgear, it was a lot more involved. Setting up outside ports was a pain; at the time, there was no simple way of forwarding ports. I recall a little workaround I was able to conduct with the server, but it took me days to figure out.

The firmware also lacks time restrictions for devices (at least of this writing). Asuswrt-Merlin allows me to set specific times to shut off internet for devices, which comes in handy with a large family.

As for the actual mesh system, so far so good. I can't tell when I'm using the main router or the satellite. The devices connect automatically without hiccup. I've since ditched Xfinity in favor of RCN 1Gbps; this mesh system works very well with the service. Once we have fiber, I can't wait to see the results.

Even after using both MX Master 2 and 3, my favorite mouse still is the Proteus Core G502. Does that mean I don't like the Master 2 or 3? Yes and no. Yes to 2, no to 3.

I prefer wired mice (yes, I said "mice"). The additional tools I get from the software for the G502 allow me to customize the G502 far more than I can with either the Master 2 or 3 (both use the same software). With dual monitors, the G502 creates for a seamless work environment. I no longer game, and still the G502 reigns supreme in my hand.

The Master 2 I received gratis from work. It was an arduous request to grant, but eventually my employer succumbed. However, I was far from impressed. I have small-ish hands for an adult, and found the Master 2 too large for comfort. I use a hybrid claw grip, and felt the Master 2 to be a ball in my hands.

But the Master 3 is a worthy upgrade that I recommend to those who are in the similar boat as me. To me, the Master 3 leveled some of that bump; now it contours comfortably to the shape of my palm. The wheel is *excellent*; while I haven't given up on my G502 wheel, I became accustomed to the Master 3 wheel faster than I did to that of the Master 2. I love the mixture of textile plastics on the Master 3. The portions that touch the palm have a rubber-like feel, while the rest comprises a harder feel.

My only qualm is the back and forward buttons. They aren't where my thumb seems to want to find them, and oftentimes I miss pressing them.

Nevertheless, this is my go-to mouse at home.
Works well for our use!

Thus far we've used this speaker while working outside, bike-riding, and at home. It does get loud enough for the family to hear the music playing while on bike rides, and is very easy to use. We've paired it with both an Android and an iPhone, and the setup was a breeze on both.
The quibble I have is that the bass can be a bit dominating. It drowns some detail in the music, even when tweaks are applied.
Works well and keeps our phones and tablets charged.
Don't use this one in tight corners. It works well and I haven't noticed any drops in speed.

We've used this primarily during the lockdown. During the summer, we were able to bust this out for at-home theater. It's not a bad projector by the cost alone, but it's not good enough. This is my first personal projector, and my experience comes from working much more expensive projectors at work.
The projector comes with a storing case, flimsy tripod, remote, and cables. The power cable is very short. If you're using this outside, be prepared to use an extension cable, even if you have an outdoor outlet near. The remote is fine, but most controls can be accessed on the projector. The tripod is very unstable. Even though it's metal, it feels very brittle and I never trust the tripod alone. With a bump, the project can move quite a bit. I therefore use a couple of books for stability.

The projector's zoom features are nonexistent; to create a smaller or bigger picture, you need to manually move the device. Not too bad, but there's a lot of fiddling around. The focus is okay; it doesn't have wide range, but we usually can find a sweet spot pretty quickly. So far we've had success connecting a Chromecast and phones, and therefore are able to watch anything that streams. The picture quality is pretty good, and seems to be right around 1080p. We've never had trouble watching anything or felt that something from the picture was out of focus. Colors seem to be adequate. There are also speakers on this thing, but, as expected, they're not very loud. Thankfully there's a 3.5mm audio jack, which we've used for external speakers.

This is our first projection screen, and we used it quite a bit this summer. It's very easy to assemble on the metal frame. It comes with legs, but we never used them; instead, we posted the screen on the back of the house.
The instructions are straight-forward; after the second assembly and disassembly, we got the hang of it very quickly and didn't need the instructions. The bag it comes with fits everything snugly, and there's even a pouch just for the screen so that it doesn't mix with the metal.
There is a very strong odor when we opened the box. Definitely has a marine smell, but it did go away after the third use.

The screen latches onto the metal frame by buttons. However, the corners are very difficult to snap on, so much so that we decided to leave them unbuttoned. Thankfully there is a surplus of buttons, so the screen stayed straight and wrinkle-free. Even with the screen folded during storage, we didn't notice any creases while watching movies in the backyard. A great investment, especially during the quarantine.

These are my first wireless ear buds. I've got a couple of $100+ IEMs, the Sony WH-1000X M3, and Audio-Technica over-the-ear headphones. I think I've got a good sense of under-$500 sound quality, and these Technics are slightly overpriced in my opinion, but they still sound fanstastic.
I have smaller ear canals than normal (as told by my audiologist), so I always opt for a size down when trying on tips. I followed the instructions to insert these Technics buds into my ear holes with the smaller tips, and they fit great. They don't come out with vigorous head-shaking, and haven't come out during my work commutes. I walk about half an hour a day, and so far so good.

The ear buds pair easily, and they always connect to my phone when I take them out of the case. I tried the noise-canceling, but found it to be sub-par compared to my Sony headphones. Sony actually sucks out the volume outside; these Technics add a white noise filter, which to me obstructs the audio I'm listening to. There's an app you can download to your phone which turns off the white-noise filter, so I did that, and turned of equalizer settings. On my phone I use Poweramp v3, AntennaPod, and Amazon Prime HD. They all sound great, but, because the Technics don't slide all the way into my ear, some of the bass gets lost. Higher volumes help, but then you run into ear damage.

Overall, I'm pleased with my first set of wireless ear buds. While they won't take over my Shure IEMs, they're super convenient to have during my work commutes.

With the right tips, these sound fantastic. I can imagine with further "break-in" and maybe some customization, they will be phenomenal. They are a little bass-heavy, but nothing too detrimental.

For reference, here's what I used:
- Samsung Note8
- VE Odyssey HD DAC
- Poweramp v3
- songs ripped from CD into FLAC using EAC

Here's my previous experience:
- 1More Quad
- Audio Technica ATH-M50x
- Sony WH-1000MX3
- Technics EAH-AZ70W

These sound better than the Technics, but not nearly as good as the Sony. With that said, these wired headphones aren't exactly the best spokesperson for staying wired. I'm all for wired for both audio and video, but I admit that wireless options like the Sony and Technics make me a believer. With the right codecs and setup, you can achieve wonderful results.

There is supreme comfort with these IEMs. With the right tips, I got them fitting snugly in my ear (but there is some trial with error), and there is a metal right around the ear to allow the wire to stay in place. But I question whether these IEMs are worth the price. For $300 you can get cheaper IEMs (imported) with better tips and cables and still have some change in your wallet. And with the push into wireless around the same price range, Shure really needs to push their technology and rely less on their name. Their name alone certainly commands attention, but the wallet is stronger.

I'm trying to transition all my USB-C cables to Thunderbolt 3, and I'm finding some brands work better than others. Monoprice, Apple, and Amazon Basics make quality, inexpensive cables. I've heard of Cable Matters, but haven't used them before. This is my first cable from them and I'm overall pleased thus far.
I ordered the short, 2.4ft since I planned on using this in the car. It's the perfect length. The plug is located just by the gear shift, and it reaches comfortably to the phone mount on the vent. It charges very quickly and stops once the phone reaches 100%. The material also seems pretty good, so I'm not worried leaving this in the car.

The qualit of this storage case is pretty darn good. The zippers are nice and thick, the fabric is thick (though I'm not sure if it will develop fuzz balls over time), and the interior is more than good. The upper half has a bumped, cushioned roof, most likely to protect anything the elastic strap hugs. The strap is also meaty and tight; I would trust the combination of the strap and cushioned roof with most electronics.
There is an abundance of plastic pages for memory cards; they seem to fit up to normal SD size. Because of this, you have to move them to access anything you may store underneath. However, because of the length of the pages, you can also opt to store things on top of them. The shell is pretty stuff (probably because of enclosed cardboard or something similar).
I haven't been able to test this cable's HDMI 2.0 capabilities yet, but for working with my Switch it works great. I've experienced no signal loss in the year-plus that I've been using it.

Basic mouse for general needs. Can come in handy during lockdown. Reminds me of the backup mice I'd purchase in my college bookstore during a night of late studying.
It works well on most surfaces, but anything with too much texture can cause it some hassle. It's also super light; I'm used to Logitech mice with weight.
These Cat7 cables work well and I haven't notice any drops in the Cat7 speeds. I like how they're very vibrant as they're easily distinguishable from other cables.

Not sure how "handmade" this laptop sleeve is, but it does the job handsomely, both functionally and aesthetically. It looks great housing my HP Pavilion in my backpack since I rarely use the sleeve by itself. It's slim but cushiony enough to provide some generous padding without taking up much space.
It doesn't feel that premium, but it otherwise looks really good.

Actual setup is pretty easy. But because there are so many parts I wouldn't recommend this as a pop-&-go solution. I'd recommend this if you want a more stable setup but easily moved to a different location. That said, once I got everything set the way I wanted, I found issues when plugging everything in. The cables are pretty thick and stiff (:wink:), which cause the connected devices to move unintentionally from their set places. So I'd suggest using lighter cables.
Otherwise, it's a fantastic set of tools you can use from taking pictures of market items to hobbyist indulgences.

I have a love/hate relationship with this device. On the one hand, it works great when it actually connects, but on the other hand I hate when it doesn't. It comes with a USB 2.0 dongle, but the keyboard can be very fidgety when connecting to the dongle. I've used this on a DE-10 Nano and Raspberry Pi 4, and they both have given me connectivity issues with this keyboard. I also tested this on a MacBook Pro, but only the mouse feature was tested (which works great).
I'm not sure if it's the battery or the keyboard, but it has a hard time staying connected. I'll lose key presses or the battery will die quickly. It becomes very upsetting when I'm resetting or entering a password and, on Raspbian, I can't see the password due to security measures, so I'll never tell if the keyboard entered the intended keys correctly until I get a success or failure. Usually when I miss a password it's due to user error, but when I'm using this keyboard it can be either user or device error.

The size of it is comfortable in the hand, and the tactility of the buttons feel great. But I feel the size is too small for it to be used as a keyboard comfortably. Some keys aren't placed in standard US ANSI layouts, and the thumb has to do quite a stretch when entering some characters or commands.

I carry around with me various cables and chargers, as well as adapters and SD cards. I used to use a roll-up organizer, but found them to be sub-optimal. I prefer book-style organizers, even though they take up more room; they're far better at organizing, and can hold more. They also tend to retain longevity of the devices since there's no stress from rolling them up.
In this case, I house a few chargers, a handful of cables, a Pelican SD card case, a power brick, additional SD cards in the included slots, and a few USB devices. I also tossed in some cable ties, even though they don't really fit anywhere. But they haven't moved around despite my moving items in and out.

The case isn't hard-shell by any means, but it does do a good job retaining its shape in my backpack. I feel it can protect my goods good enough; by adding smaller chargers in the inside spine, it helps give it a sturdier feel by adding a backbone to the spine.

This is a pretty good cable in that it can charge up to 3A using USB-A and USB-C, but the braiding on it is super stiff. It's not that flexible, so it doesn't work well with tight areas or if you've got the cable connected to a narrow port.
Still, for the actual charging and syncing it works well.

I've had Verbatim products since I was a wee lad in the '90s and my parents had Verbatim 3.5" disks. The name is a good name for easy-to-find computer storage options, and the name still does well today.
I've used this 2.5" SATA SSD in myriad devices, from a hard drive bay to a Linux laptop, and it currently resides in my PS3 Slim where the OS boots a bit faster than the previous, stock HDD (though not much faster since the PS3 doesn't support SSD natively). No matter how many times I've wiped or used this SSD, the product works well. It's got a nice, satin shell that allows it to fit in all kinds of devices.

I use this bay for two semi-permanent WD Blue drives, as well as the occasional SSD. I've never had the bay fail on me in over a year of use. The cable is pretty short, but then again I have the bay pretty far from the computer. Because I don't have a desktop, bays and enclosures come really handy for me.
Sometimes the bay falls asleep after a period of inactivity; it can take up to 15 seconds for it to awake fully, but a minor issue considering how much use I've gotten out of it.
Because of this as well as a Sabrent hub I have, I'm a fan of their products.

I'm currently using this with my NextcloudPi setup to store my own data over the network. The Raspberry Pi4 supports USB 3.0, which this SSD also does. That's one of the main things I look for when hounding an SSD: fast transfer rates, as well as large capacity.
I know Samsung has a good reputation for SSD storage; I was very excited when this came in the mail. After re-installing NextcloudPi, I let the setup wizard reformat the Samsung T7 into Btrfs. The T7 formated flawlessly, and the storage shows up completely on both my web panel and my web settings.

I had to restart my Pi4 a few times, and each time I shot some items to my SSD for testing. I noticed it was pretty slow on boot, but after a few hours it seemed to read and write almost as fast as my previous SSD. I supposed, over time, it will adjust to the Pi4. My previous drive was a Verbatim USB SSD, also 3.0. That thing got HOT. It was also made of aluminum on the outside, and I was afraid this T7 would be the same. So far so good; it remains much cooler than the Verbatim.

I hope laptops don't go the way of phones where they try to get rid of as many features for the sake of thinness. Computers are tools and if you can't use a computer to its fullest then it's not made correctly. Unfortunately, our family as a newer MBP and I'm constantly attaching this hub just to plug in USB devices, SD cards, and now a LAN cable since I'm trying to set up hotspots around the home.

The ports for the USB and cards are fast, and I like that there are both dedicated 2.0 and 3.0 ports. I also like that there's a dedicated microSD slot, since most of my SD cards nowadays are microSD; if I'm multi-taskin' then I can place two cards, one with an adapter and one without.

The LAN port is a bit sluggish in comparison. It takes a while to detect internet via Ethernet cable, and sometimes it spots out.
I used these when my trusty Velcro-branded ties ran out. They're a bit too wide and thin for my taste, but they do the job. They haven't ripped at all!
We got this to carry around our MBP. It works well and has great cushion. It is a bit bulky and takes up some room in bags, but by itself it works great and resists a lot of stains.

This is the first time I've considered a build, and I was fortunate to receive this to put in. It was very easy install, but as I mentioned I'm a newb and therefore am not sure if ease of installation is usually as simple. The lights are pretty easy to control as well.
The lights are pretty unobtrusive, and it seems to work great overall. It's quiet and the lighting is subtle in my case.

We had an Asus router that was working extremely well over the past couple of years, but for some reason it just went completely kaputt. Finally, it was time to set this one up.
The installation was a breeze, and I love that there's an app to allow me to monitor it instead of having to use a web browser. However, the initial web page needs some updating!
I'm pretty tech-savvy, but IT stuff always gets me hot and bothered. This one was one of the better experiences.

So far so good, but I will update if I need to change my rating.

Love the bold red cable as it makes it easier to spot amongst the tangle of black and white cables we have. The first week I had it I carried it in my Switch case, and used it for both my Switch and Note8. Worked great. Tested it on our 2016 MBP as well and it worked fine; didn't charge as quickly as Apple's own charger, but for USB 3.1 it charged fast enough.

Now I keep it in my car as my car charger for my phone while driving. The cable is long enough to reach the USB ports in the middle console, but I'm able to leave it in the adapter near the front console while the phone is held on by the vent mount. The included strap helps keep the braided cable in place.
The ends seem to be made of very strong metal (aluminum?). There are Amazon Basics logos on them, but time will tell how long they last.

This is an extremely nice stand, and goes well with any desk setup and any laptop. I currently use it at work to prop my black Dell work laptop, and it still looks nice with a mostly black computer setup. The aluminum feels a bit on the cheap side, but still decent enough. It's very sturdy and gives me the assurance this will last some years, if not decades. You have to assemble it out of the box, but it comes with the hex key you need (as most assembly-required items do anyway these days).

It rotates fine and doesn't swivel when it's not supposed to. I'm able to plug items in and out of the laptop and it doesn't move at all, but when I want to swivel it it has enough give when I push. The only nitpick I have is that I sometimes havce to move the laptop up a bit to open it as there no support in the back. I realize that's to accomodate laptops of many sizes, but if they implemented a back panel that could slide in and out of the support panel then that would've negated having to lift the laptop up. I tned to power off my computer during the weekends, so every Monday morning I have to stretch awkwardly over my desk, prop the laptop up to open it and power it on, then rest it back down. Again, not really a dealbreaker but it's the only thing from making this stand perfect in my eyes.

And I mean really hot! I can't even touch it when it's plugged in, let alone when data is being transferred. Still, it's super fast. My computer recognizes it and opens it immediately after plugging it in, and data transfers extremely quickly. Helps that my USB port is USB 3.0 as well.
The color is nice, but the metal is a bit too glossy for being matte. The cable is very short but works fine enough for me. Just be warned that you can't touch this when it's being used!

A mixture of white and aluminum normally goes okay but doesn't really work here. The white color of the plastic doesn't seem to blend well with the aluminum pole of the stand. They do work well with my Sony noise-canceling headphones at work, but they do not look pleasant with my work setup. You have to assemble the base by placing the holder and the base into the pole, and that's pretty much it. I wouldn't choose these again if I had the choice, though.

We have a cable box in the living room, but it's costly to add smaller boxes, so we opted for this to use in the bedroom. Thankfully, our bedroom TV is a smart TV so we can stream most things, but it's still nice to have local channels to catch the news. Our building is an older building with plaster walls, so I was afraid this wasn't going to work as well. The bedroom TV is against a wall that's in the middle of the apartment; once I set everything up, however, I was shocked to find that it still worked well. It's not a simple plug-and-play; after everything is plugged in, you have to run an initialization through the TV's menu (which the antenanna insturctions dictate, but I chose to ignore the first time around). There are a lot more channels than I thought there'd be; after the first initialization process, all the channels stay there. I've had no issues with it getting a good signal. I think being on the very top level of my apartment building helps, even though the walls are plaster.
The only downside is that the channel selection is backwards on my TV. I can't tell if it's my TV or the antenna. When changing channels and pressing up, the mini guide shows the channels going down. It's a bit confusing, even months after using this.

This isn't the first time I've installed memory, but I was super excited to try these. The colors are vibrant but can be controlled easily, and they go very well with the Corsair RGB CPU cooler I have. The enhancement stronger RAM provides is always a must, and this is no exception. I know RGB may be a bit flashy for some people, but I embrace the vibrancy.

These wireless headphones were easy to set up with my iPhone. I usually use them while using the elliptical at the gym. The earbuds stay in my ear. One drawback is that they are not especially comfortable - the earbuds aren’t soft. I’m usually only using them for about 30 minutes at a time but I could see them becoming extremely uncomfortable with prolonged use - so I decreased my review by one star.
The color of the earbuds is nice and the sound is clear. The batteries last a decent amount of time. I usually charge them prior to each time I use them though.

At the time I received this remote with my new X1 box, it was the first "smart" remote we had in the household; I was fiddling with the remote, box, and TV for a whole night to soak in all the features. My favorite to this day is how intelligent the lighting is on the buttons; lift them slightly and the lights turn on, but remain off when lying still for a while.

I haven't used the voice features after the initial night, so I can't comment on that. Everything still works great, and overall I find the button configuration pretty intuitive. I still confuse the Exit and Last buttons sometimes, so maybe some tweaking could be used between those two (if there hasn't been yet). But the main issue I have is how the power buttons don't work properly. When turning on both box and TV, the TV will turn on but the X1 box won't. It's been like that with two TVs. And when powering them off the TV will turn off but the box won't. I have to manually turn it off, which is a step more than I'd like but I've adjusted.

This is specifically made for iPhone 6/6s. It also comes with a case. You have to be within 150 feet of the item in order for it to be detected. In order for this to work, you have to use the case provided or the pixie needs to attach to your current case. I love my current case so I didn’t not opt to use the included case. The pixie that comes to attach to your current phone case is bulky and not very secretive.
My phone paired easily. When opening the app, it shows the location of the item where the pixie was last updated. The pixie is very similar to the Tile locator, but I prefer the look of the Tile moreso.

I knew right away that these would be my office headphones. I have a mechanical keyboard that I use at work, and the office I work in is semi-open. There's a *lot* of noise coming every-which-way. These are a much-needed accessory to my work productivity, as I'm easily distracted by things in my periphery, whether visually or auditory.

The presentation is great. The box is very high quality, reminiscent of the recent Samsung Galaxy device boxes. A smooth matte feel with gloss--weirdly pristine. The box slides out of the slipcover and you get the headphones already in the case. What I like is that they're folded, and there's even a little sheet underneath the phones that always reminds you how to put them back in. Also included is a 3.5mm cable in case you don't want to use Bluetooth, a charging cable, and an adapter. The case is nice, but as I keep mine at work I can't testify to its durability. There's a thin mesh net on the backside in case anyone needs to store one or two thin headphone accessory/-ies along. The accent colors are a nice light copper/rose gold color. I love that color; I'm glad it's getting more attention in recent years.

It didn't take long to charge the headphones, so they come with a little bit of juice. As soon as you turn them on, you get a soft beep along with a voice indicating they're turned on. Nice responsive feedback. Once I put them on I could hear the headphones working to drown out the sound; there was a thick veil of soundproofing that was draped over my ears as soon as the earpads touched them.

The first thing I did was listen to podcasts through the Pocket Casts app and .flac music through Poweramp v3. With podcasts, the difference was phenomenal. Listening to "Wait, wait... Don't tell me!" made me feel as though I were in the audience. The music was fantastic...until I tried on my other headphones which I use for music only.
I thought the bass might've been too strong with the Sony headphones, and I was right. After using even "cheaper" headphones like the Audio-Technica M50x, I could tell the Sony had too much bass. I'm not sure if that's partly because of the noise-canceling technology or what, but the bass can be toned down a bit, methinks.

I then proceeded to download the supplementary app to get the fullest suite of attributes the headphones can get. The app works well, and I didn't experience any hiccups while actually using the app. The only hiccup was when I was trying to download the update. It took *forever*. Almost an hour and it was just halfway through. I decided to bring them to work the next day and let the app sit there while updating. Thankfully, it remembers the progress, even though the app kept crashing during the update process.

There are some optimization tweaks in the app, some sound profiles to let you configure the noise cancelation level (yes, level; the noise cancelation is pure software; you can set it to drown out the most noise as possible or have no noise cancellation at all), and even a little snippet of what is currently playing through the headphones. A simple UI with all the features you need.

The first few days I used it I was active, and I kept noticing that my ears sometimes would pop depending on whether I sat down or arose quickly. Another weird thing is that when I take the headphones off, my ears sometimes need a minute or two to adjust. There's so much noise in the world! After taking the headphones off I can hear HVAC activity and my loud work neighbor who's otherwise not that loud.

I had some headphones with some touch controls before and always found them tacky. I used them once when I first got them and never again. But with these headphones, I'm always using the tap gesture to play/pause and the swipe gesture to raise or lower the volume. There are also swipe gestures to skip or go back a track, but since I never do that anyway I never use those gestures. You have to be careful with the tap; when it works, it works. But the whole surface isn't the active portion and you have to hit it right in the center. Sometimes I'm hitting my finger against my ears trying to find the spot and hurting myself in the process. I tested the gesture where you put your entire palm on the cup to turn off the noise canceling feature and let the mic allow incoming conversation, but not after the third try. I could hear the other people just fine, but I found the right hand over my ear felt awkward, and one person didn't realize I could even hear them. Putting your hand over your headphones isn't a gesture people immediately see as you paying attention to them.

The headphones are extremely lightweight and comfortable to use; I left them on for about two hours once before having to take them off. I actually was surprised with how light they were; when I got the Amazon box I didn't believe it was my headphones. It was much lighter than expected.

For my first noise-canceling headphones I'm pleased. The sound balance can be better (less bass), but they make for fantastic headphones to use at work. I wasn't sure what I was expecting with noise-canceling technology. I thought it would drown out all noises, but you still can hear the occasional mutter; it just won't be distinct.

Oh, forgot to mention the battery life. I charged it only once and have been using it for a week, at about an hour or two each day. Still going well. If you press the power button once it will tell you the battery level. AFter the initial update the voice indicator might give the wrong battery level (it did for me), but give it about ten or fifteen minutes to adjust and it will go back to normal.

Have this plugged in in one of the main sockets in the kitchen. The wall outlet is the only one away from liquids, so it's the only one I felt safe plugging this into. Unfortunately, that outlet plate shares space with a switch, and this surge protector presses against the switch so that it bends it a bit. There's no damage, but I did have to force this a bit in there to get it situated. Would be nice if GE engineered it so that it was less than half the size of a square plate.

The plugs work fine, however. We've used it for a few kitchen appliances and a vacuum cleaner, all plugged in at the same time, and about three running at once while charging a phone, and the power kept up fine. Very handy to have in a room where people constantly charge phones and tablets, but that also requires other plugged items like appliances.

Now that I'm transitioning to a more corporate world I figured it's about time I get a more "professional"-looking carrying satchel than my Osprey backpack. The only laptops I possess range around thirteen inches, as I find carrying anything heavier than that is far too large to be considered portable.

This briefcase has it all. There are pockets galore; at times I feel there are too many as I keep unzipping the wrong pocket or can't remember in which pocket I put something, so I wish the tags would've been different somehow. Maybe have some lanyards on some or another.

But inside the pockets you get even more pockets and sashes to separate compartments. The material is sturdy and has held up just fine in this insane Chicago spring weather. We've had temperatures ranging from 40-80 in just two weeks, as well as rainy and dry weathers. Chicago, I tell ya!
My 2010 13" MBP fits fine in the main laptop sleeve without sliding around much, and I'm not able to feel much wait on my shoulder from carrying it around all day, along with a couple of books, a Hobonichi planner, and my pencil case.

The main flaw I will say this has is the shoulder strap. It's not easily adjustable, and I still haven't fully figured it out. There is a buckle in the middle on either side--one static, and the other adjustable. But the adjustable buckle doesn't allow the strap easy give, and so I can't for the life of me get it to a comfortable length.
The removable strap is sturdy otherwise.

The other issue is the clasp holding the two handles together. It's not long enough, so instead of closing it with one hand I'm having to use both hands to squeeze the handles together before being able to snap the button together.

All in all, it's a great briefcase usable even with 13" laptops, but the shoulder strap and the handle clasp need better, user-friendly improvements.

Good sound quality but not the best for noise cancellation. It is inconvenient they are not foldable and, considering so, they should at least come with a case. Fit feels snug and they have not fallen off on accident. Bluetooth range is very good, I have been able to walk 3 floors down in my house and did not lose connection.

Nice lanyard to have on the backpack. Perfect for charging most mobile devices as we transition to USB-C as the standard. The plug ends are inserted into a cap with a thin lanyard. That then gets screwed in so the plugs don't fall out.
I found that the thin lanyard attached to the cap was a bit too thin; not sure how it will be in the long run, but compared to the very thick strand at the bottom it seemed odd to have such a thin one at the top.
